sections.heading: What Is CGSOS? - Chhattisgarh State Open School Overview

content.text: The Chhattisgarh State Open School (CGSOS) is the official open schooling authority for the state of Chhattisgarh, functioning under the Chhattisgarh Board of Secondary Education (CGBSE). It provides secondary and higher secondary level education to students who, for various reasons, are unable to attend regular schools including working adults, dropouts, and those seeking a second chance at formal education.

CGSOS offers flexibility in terms of subject selection, study pace, and exam attempts, making it a popular choice for thousands of learners across Chhattisgarh every year. sections.heading: Important Tips for CGSOS 2026 Exam Preparation

content.text: With the CGSOS 2026 exams kicking off on 10 August, students now have a clear timeline to organize their study plan. Here are some practical and effective preparation strategies tailored for open school students:
Plan a Subject-Wise Study Timetable

Use the date sheet above to work backwards from each exam date. Allocate more revision days to high-weightage or difficult subjects like Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, and Accountancy. Easier or language-based papers (Hindi, English, Sanskrit) can be prepared in shorter revision windows.
Focus on CGSOS Syllabus and Sample Papers

Students should always study from the official CGSOS syllabus for 2025-26. Practicing previous year question papers and sample papers is one of the most effective strategies for scoring well. These give a clear idea of the question pattern, marking scheme, and important topics.
Prioritize Gap Days Wisely

The CGSOS 2026 schedule has several built-in gap days between exams (e.g., no exams on 12, 14-16, 23, 26, and 28 August). These breaks should be used productively for revision, solving mock tests, and addressing weak areas not for complete rest.
Stay Updated with Official Announcements

The exam schedule can occasionally be revised due to administrative or unforeseen reasons. Students must regularly check the official CGBSE/CGSOS website and keep an eye on official announcements. Also verify the exam center details printed on your admit card.
Keep Documents Ready
Students must carry their CGSOS Admit Card 2026 and a valid photo ID to every exam center. Without the admit card, entry to the examination hall will be denied.

sections.heading: What Is CG PET 2026? A Quick Overview

content.text: Before diving into the result and answer key details, here is a brief overview of the CG PET exam for candidates who need context.

The Chhattisgarh Pre Engineering Test (CG PET) is a prestigious state-level engineering entrance examination conducted by the Chhattisgarh Vyavasayik Pariksha Mandal (CG Vyapam). It serves as the gateway for admission to the following undergraduate programmes in government and private colleges across Chhattisgarh:

The CG PET 2026 examination was conducted as a pen-and-paper (offline) based test from 10:00 AM to 1:15 PM at 33 district headquarters across Chhattisgarh, covering subjects of Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics.

sections.heading: CG PET 2026 - Key Dates at a Glance

content.text: This section provides a consolidated timeline of all important events related to CG PET 2026, from the application phase to result and counselling. Keeping track of these dates ensures you do not miss any critical deadline.
Important: All candidates are advised to regularly check vyapamcg.cgstate.gov.in for the latest updates, as exact dates are officially notified on the portal.

sections.heading: Understanding the CG PET 2026 Final Answer Key

content.text: The final answer key is the officially validated set of correct answers published by CG Vyapam after reviewing all candidate objections raised against the provisional key. Here is what candidates need to know about it.

sections.heading: What Is the Difference Between Provisional and Final Answer Key?

items: The provisional answer key is released shortly after the exam and is open for challenges.
Candidates can raise objections - called "Dava Aapatti" - by paying a fee of ₹50 per challenge.
After reviewing all objections, CG Vyapam releases the final answer key, which is the authoritative version.
The final answer key is directly used to calculate every candidate's score and prepare the merit list.
No further objections are accepted against the final answer key.

sections.heading: What If a Question Is Found Incorrect?

content.text: If any question in the CG PET 2026 paper is found to be incorrect or dropped after the objection review process, all candidates are awarded marks for that question regardless of their response. In the 2025 edition, for example, four questions were dropped by the board and marks were awarded to all candidates.

sections.heading: No Negative Marking in CG PET

content.text: A significant advantage of the CG PET examination pattern is that there is no negative marking for incorrect or unattempted answers. Each correct answer carries marks based on the official key.

sections.heading: How to Check CG PET 2026 Result and Download Scorecard

content.text: Checking the CG PET 2026 result is a straightforward online process. Follow the step-by-step guide below to access your scorecard without any confusion.

items: Visit the official CG Vyapam website: vyapamcg.cgstate.gov.in
Navigate to the "Results" or "CG PET 2026 Result" link on the homepage.
Log in using your Vyapam profile credentials (Registration Number and Date of Birth).
Your CG PET 2026 result and scorecard will appear on the screen.
Download and save the scorecard - it is mandatory for the counselling and admission process.
Take a printout for future reference.

sections.heading: What Details Are Shown on the CG PET 2026 Scorecard?

content.text: Your CG PET 2026 scorecard will contain the following details:

items: Candidate's Name, Roll Number, and Registration Number
Father's and Mother's Name
Date of Birth and Category
Subject-wise Marks (Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics) - out of 50 marks each
Total Marks Obtained
Merit Rank

sections.heading: CG PET 2026 Merit List - What You Need to Know

content.text: The merit list is one of the most closely watched documents published alongside the CG PET 2026 result. This section explains who makes it to the merit list and what information it contains.

sections.heading: Minimum Qualifying Marks for CG PET 2026

content.text: To be included in the CG PET merit list and become eligible for counselling, candidates must clear the minimum qualifying threshold:
The final qualifying marks are officially notified by CG Vyapam and may vary slightly each year. Candidates must confirm the exact threshold on the official website.

sections.heading: What Does the Merit List Include?

content.text: The CG PET 2026 merit list contains the following details for each qualified candidate:

items: Roll Number and Application Number
Candidate's Full Name
Category and Class Type
Gender and Date of Birth
Disability Status (if applicable)
Domicile Status
Total Marks Obtained and Merit Rank

sections.heading: After the Result: CG PET 2026 Counselling Process

content.text: Clearing the CG PET 2026 exam is only the first step. The actual seat allotment happens through the counselling process conducted by the Directorate of Technical Education (DTE), Chhattisgarh. Here is a complete overview of what comes next.

sections.heading: Overview of Counselling Rounds

content.text: CG PET counselling is typically held in 3 to 4 rounds, including spot rounds, scheduled from June to August 2026. Two separate phases of counselling are conducted:

items: Phase 1 - For Government and Government-Aided Colleges
Phase 2 - For Private Colleges

sections.heading: Step-by-Step Counselling Process

items: Counselling Registration - Register on the DTE Chhattisgarh counselling portal (separate from the CG Vyapam exam portal).
Choice Filling - Select your preferred colleges and courses in order of preference.
Seat Allotment - Seats are allotted based on CG PET rank, category, and choices filled.
Document Verification - Report to the allotted college or designated centre for document verification.
Reporting and Admission - Report to the allotted institute and complete the admission formalities.

content.text: Important: Missing the counselling registration deadline means losing your seat even if your rank is strong. Act promptly once the result is declared.

sections.heading: Documents Required for CG PET Counselling

content.text: Ensure all the following documents are self-attested and ready before counselling registration opens:

items: CG PET 2026 Scorecard / Rank Card
Class 10th and 12th Mark Sheets and Passing Certificates
Category Certificate (OBC/SC/ST, if applicable)
Domicile Certificate (mandatory for Chhattisgarh state quota seats)
Transfer Certificate (TC) from the last attended institution
Character Certificate
Passport-size Photographs
Photo ID Proof (Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, etc.)
Disability Certificate (if applicable)

sections.heading: Who Can Apply for Admission via CG PET 2026?

content.text: The CG PET 2026 serves students from Chhattisgarh as well as candidates from other states. Notably, candidates from other states can also apply for admission through JEE Main scores as an alternative pathway. Chhattisgarh domicile holders are eligible for the state quota seats during counselling.

sections.heading: Re-Evaluation Policy: Can You Challenge the Result?

content.text: A common question among candidates is whether re-evaluation of the answer sheet is possible. CG Vyapam evaluates all OMR answer sheets through a machine-based automated process aligned with the final answer key. Due to this, re-evaluation of the OMR sheet is not provided. However, candidates are encouraged to challenge any incorrect answer during the provisional answer key objection window (Dava Aapatti), which is the only official avenue for raising concerns before the result is finalised.

sections.heading: CA Foundation Passing Marks 2026

content.text: To pass the CA Foundation examination, candidates must score at least 40 marks out of 100 in each of the four papers and at least 200 marks out of 400 in aggregate.
Both conditions must be satisfied. Obtaining 200 or more marks in total is not sufficient if a candidate fails to secure the prescribed minimum marks in an individual paper.

sections.heading: CA Foundation September 2026 Result - Paper-Wise Marks

content.text: The Foundation examination consists of four papers, each carrying 100 marks.
Candidates should review their scorecards to understand their performance in each paper and whether they have satisfied both the paper-wise and aggregate qualifying requirements.

content.text: ICAI has declared the Foundation result. Candidates should refer to ICAI’s official examination statistics for the number of candidates who appeared, the number who passed and the pass percentage when these figures are published or verified.
The statistics may include the number of candidates who appeared, the number who passed and the overall pass percentage.
An official September 2026 Foundation pass-percentage figure has not been independently verified for this article. Figures from earlier sessions should not be presented as September 2026 statistics.

sections.heading: ICAI CA Foundation Toppers List 2026

sections.heading: CA Foundation Result 2026 - Is There a Separate Cut Off?

content.text: The primary qualifying requirements for the CA Foundation examination are the prescribed minimum marks in each paper and the overall aggregate.

These requirements are different from a competitive recruitment examination in which selection may depend on a vacancy-based cut-off. Candidates should refer to ICAI's examination rules for the applicable passing standard rather than relying on speculative cut-off predictions.

sections.heading: What Happens After CA Foundation Result 2026?

content.text: Candidates who pass the September 2026 CA Foundation examination can proceed towards the Chartered Accountancy Intermediate course, subject to ICAI's applicable course-registration and training requirements.
Candidates who do not qualify may consider appearing in a subsequent Foundation examination session, following the Institute's registration and examination-application rules.
All candidates should retain their result information and follow the official ICAI Student Services Portal for further course-related instructions.

sections.heading: CA Foundation January 2027 Examination

content.text: ICAI's next Foundation examination session is scheduled for January 2027. Candidates planning to appear in that session should follow the official examination application schedule and eligibility instructions.
The January 2027 examination application window opened on 3 November 2026, with the regular application deadline reported as 16 November 2026 and the late-fee deadline as 19 November 2026.
These dates relate to the next examination session, not the September 2026 result declaration.

content.text: ICSE Class 10 Economics Syllabus 2026-27 covers six major units for students preparing for the ICSE 2027 board examination. The syllabus includes The Productive Mechanism, Theory of Demand and Supply, Market, Banking in India, Inflation and Consumer Awareness. The Economics examination carries 80 marks in theory and 20 marks in internal assessment, with a two-hour written paper.

Students should prepare the complete chapter-wise syllabus, including important economic concepts, demand and supply curves, banking functions, inflation and consumer rights. The Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE) publishes its official syllabuses through cisce.org. Candidates should select the syllabus labelled Examination Year 2027.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Syllabus 2026-27 Chapter-Wise

content.text: The Economics syllabus for the ICSE Class 10 examination covers six major units. Each unit contains several concepts and subtopics that students should prepare.

rows: Land, Labour, Capital, Entrepreneur and Factors of Production
Demand, Supply, Curves, Laws, Elasticity and Determinants
Perfect Competition, Monopoly, Monopolistic Competition and Oligopoly
Money, Commercial Banks, Central Bank, Monetary Policy and Public Finance
Stages, Types, Causes and Effects of Inflation
Consumer Rights, Consumer Protection, RTI, PDS and Quality Certification

sections.heading: Unit 1: The Productive Mechanism

content.text: This unit introduces the four major factors of production and explains their contribution to economic activities.

sections.heading: Important Topics

items: Meaning and characteristics of land as a factor of production.
Productivity of land and factors affecting land productivity.
Meaning and characteristics of labour.
Division of labour, its types and advantages.
Efficiency of labour and reasons for low labour efficiency in India.
Meaning and characteristics of capital.
Physical and financial capital with examples.
Capital formation, its process and importance.
Meaning of entrepreneur.
Functions of an entrepreneur and contribution to economic development.

content.text: Students should understand the differences among land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship and explain how each contributes to production.

sections.heading: Unit 2: Theory of Demand and Supply

content.text: This unit examines how consumer demand and market supply are related to price and other economic factors.

sections.heading: Important Topics

items: Meaning and concept of demand and supply.
Types of demand.
Law of demand and law of supply.
Individual and market demand schedules.
Individual and market supply schedules.
Demand and supply curves.
Movement along demand and supply curves.
Shift in demand and supply curves.
Determinants of demand and supply.
Exceptions to the law of demand.
Meaning and types of elasticity of demand.
Meaning and types of elasticity of supply.
Percentage method of measuring price elasticity.
Factors affecting elasticity of demand and supply.

content.text: Students should practise drawing and interpreting demand and supply curves and clearly distinguish a movement along a curve from a shift of the entire curve.

Important: The accessible CISCE Economics syllabus reference specifies that numerical problems on elasticity are not for testing. Students should follow the corresponding instructions in their Examination Year 2027 document when preparing.

sections.heading: Unit 3: Market

content.text: The Market unit covers the meaning of a market and the different types of market structures.

rows: A Market with Many Buyers and Sellers
A Market with a Single Seller
Competition Among Sellers Offering Differentiated Products
A Market Dominated by a Small Number of Sellers

sections.heading: Unit 4: Banking in India

content.text: Banking in India is a broad unit that includes money, commercial banks, central banking, monetary policy and public finance.

sections.heading: Money

items: Barter system and its limitations.
Evolution and legal meaning of money.
Money as a medium of exchange.
Money as a measure of value.
Money as a store of value.
Money as a standard of deferred payment.

sections.heading: Commercial Banks

items: Meaning and functions of commercial banks.
Types of bank deposits.
Types of loans and methods of advancing loans.
Basic process of credit creation.
Primary and derivative deposits.

sections.heading: Central Bank and Monetary Policy

items: Meaning and functions of the central bank.
Issue of currency notes.
Banker's bank and lender of last resort.
Banker, agent and adviser to the government.
Custodian of foreign exchange.
Qualitative credit control methods, including moral suasion, margin requirements and credit rationing.
Quantitative credit control methods, including Bank Rate, Open Market Operations, Cash Reserve Ratio and Statutory Liquidity Ratio.
Basic understanding of demonetisation.

sections.heading: Public Finance

items: Meaning of public finance.
Sources of public revenue.
Direct and indirect taxes and their differences.
Meaning and objectives of Goods and Services Tax (GST).
Progressive, proportional, regressive and degressive taxes.
Non-tax revenue with examples.
Public expenditure and its classification.
Revenue expenditure and capital expenditure.
Reasons for increasing public expenditure.
Meaning and types of public debt.

content.text: Students should particularly practise comparison questions covering commercial banks and central banks, qualitative and quantitative credit controls, and direct and indirect taxation.

sections.heading: Unit 5: Inflation

content.text: This unit focuses on the meaning, categories, causes and economic effects of inflation.

sections.heading: Important Topics

items: Meaning of inflation.
Creeping inflation.
Walking inflation.
Running inflation.
Hyperinflation.
Demand-pull inflation.
Cost-push inflation.
Causes of demand-pull and cost-push inflation.
Differences between the two main types of inflation.
Negative effects of inflation on production.
Effects of inflation on fixed-income earners and business-income groups.

content.text: Students should understand the differences among inflation types and explain their effects using simple examples.

sections.heading: Unit 6: Consumer Awareness

content.text: The final unit deals with consumer exploitation, rights, duties and protection mechanisms.

sections.heading: Important Topics

items: Meaning of consumer exploitation.
Forms and reasons for consumer exploitation.
Meaning and importance of consumer awareness.
Consumer rights and consumer duties.
Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
Right to Information (RTI).
Food adulteration and its harmful effects.
Public Distribution System (PDS).
Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS).
AGMARK certification.
ECOMARK certification.

content.text: Students should be able to explain how consumer rights, consumer protection laws and standardisation marks help protect buyers.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Exam Pattern 2027

content.text: The Economics examination combines a written theory paper with an internal project or assignment.

The official subject syllabus specifies the overall assessment division. Students should refer to the specimen question paper for the question format, section-wise choices and applicable marking instructions.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Chapter-Wise Marks Distribution

content.text: The syllabus establishes the six required units but does not provide a confirmed fixed marks allocation for each individual chapter.
Students should not assume that every unit carries equal marks or rely on unofficial chapter-wise weightage tables as guaranteed examination allocations.
Prepare all six units and use the official specimen papers and previous examination papers to understand the expected question format.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Internal Assessment 2026-27

content.text: Students must complete at least one Economics project or assignment prescribed by their teacher.
The internal assessment carries 20 marks. The subject teacher and an external examiner assess the project independently.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics Project Topics

content.text: The published syllabus provides project and assignment examples related to factors of production, taxation and GST.

sections.heading: Project 1: Factors of Production

content.text: Visit a local industrial unit and study how land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship are combined in the production process.

sections.heading: Project 2: Survey on Taxes

content.text: Conduct a survey of 15 people in the neighbourhood to study the types of taxes they pay. Analyse which type of tax respondents find easier to pay and explain the conclusion.

sections.heading: Project 3: Impact of GST

content.text: Visit a nearby store and select five commonly purchased products. Examine the impact of GST on their prices or demand and discuss the benefits or implications for producers, consumers and the government.
The final project topic, submission format and assessment requirements should be confirmed with the school's Economics teacher.

sections.heading: How to Download ICSE Class 10 Economics Syllabus 2026-27?

items: Visit the official CISCE website at cisce.org.
Open the syllabus or regulations and syllabuses section.
Select the ICSE examination.
Choose the syllabus corresponding to Examination Year 2027.
Find Economics under the Group II subjects.
Open the Economics (64) syllabus document.
Verify that its cover or page headings refer to Examination Year 2027.
Download and save the PDF for examination preparation.

sections.heading: ICSE Class 10 Economics 2026-27 Preparation Tips

items: Begin preparation with the six units listed in the syllabus.
Learn important definitions and distinguish closely related economic concepts.
Practise demand and supply schedules and curves.
Prepare comparison tables for different market structures.
Understand banking functions, GST and monetary policy terminology.
Revise inflation types, their causes and effects.
Learn consumer rights, duties and important consumer protection measures.
Complete the Economics project according to the teacher's instructions.
Use official specimen and past examination papers for revision.
Revise the complete syllabus instead of relying on unverified chapter weightage.

sections.heading: Difference Between ICSE Economics and Economic Applications

content.text: ICSE Economics and Economic Applications are separate subjects with different subject codes and syllabus requirements.

The schedule contains the dates for registration, payment, choice filling, choice locking, seat allotment processing, result publication, institute reporting and verification of joined candidates.
The counselling process consists of three regular rounds followed by two stray vacancy rounds for remaining seats.

AIAPGET-qualified candidates should read the official information bulletin before registering because the fee requirements, security deposit rules, eligibility conditions and withdrawal penalties differ according to the counselling stage.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Eligibility Criteria

content.text: Candidates seeking AACCC postgraduate counselling must have qualified in AIAPGET 2026 and satisfy the applicable academic and institutional admission conditions.
The counselling covers eligible MD/MS postgraduate programmes in Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathy.
Admission is subject to the relevant entrance examination merit, qualifying degree, internship requirements, institutional eligibility and applicable regulatory provisions.
Final eligibility is verified by the allotted institution. Merely registering for counselling does not guarantee a postgraduate seat.

content.text: Round 1 choice filling begins on 27 October and ends on 1 November 2026 at 11:55 PM.
Choice locking will be available on 1 November from 2 PM to 11:55 PM.
Candidates should check the available college and course options, confirm the applicable fees and arrange preferences according to their actual admission choices.
Once choices are locked, AACCC does not allow candidates to modify them. Students should therefore review the college, course and preference order carefully.
Earlier-round choices do not automatically remain valid for all subsequent counselling rounds. Candidates must submit fresh choices where required under the counselling scheme.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Round 1 Seat Allotment Result

content.text: AACCC will process the first-round seat allotment on 2 November 2026 and publish the result on 3 November 2026.
The allotment will be determined according to the applicable candidate merit, eligibility, preferences, category and available seats.
Candidates who receive seats should download the individual allotment information through the official portal and complete the prescribed joining formalities between 4 and 13 November.

sections.heading: AIAPGET Counselling 2026 Reporting and Admission Confirmation

content.text: After seat allotment, eligible candidates must report to the allotted institution within the scheduled reporting period.
The college will verify the candidate's academic qualifications, examination result, internship and category-related documents, where applicable.
AACCC instructs students to obtain an online-generated provisional admission letter after completing physical reporting.
Admission confirmation and any subsequent relieving or withdrawal must be processed through the official AACCC system. Offline changes are not recognised under the counselling scheme.

content.text: The final document checklist depends on the candidate's course, category and allotted institution. Students must follow the current official information bulletin and college-specific instructions.

content.text: The registration fee is non-refundable. The security deposit may be refunded after completion of the counselling process if the candidate satisfies the refund conditions.

AACCC states that security money can be forfeited if a candidate does not join an allotted seat in Round 2 or later rounds, withdraws contrary to the counselling rules, or fails to comply with prescribed conditions.

There is no free exit from an allotted Round 3 or stray vacancy seat under the specified rules. Withdrawal or non-joining can also make a candidate ineligible for further AYUSH postgraduate counselling.

content.text: Once ICAI activates the admit card link, candidates can download their CA Final November 2026 hall ticket through the official examination services portal. Follow these steps:

items: Visit the ICAI examination services portal at eservices.icai.org.
Find the admit card download link for the CA Final November 2026 examination.
Open the relevant login page.
Enter the registration details and password requested by the portal.
Submit the details to access the admit card.
Check your name, roll number, examination group, centre and paper dates.
Download the hall ticket in PDF format.
Take a clear printout for the examination.

sections.heading: ICAI CA Final November 2026 Group-Wise Exam Dates
Important Instructions

items: Download only from the official portal. Log in at eservices.icai.org with your Self Service Portal credentials, then go to Exams and select the Final November 2026 admit card. ICAI releases the hall ticket online only, with no physical copy by post.
Carry a printout and photo ID. Take a printed A4 admit card and a valid government photo ID. You can’t enter the exam hall without the admit card.
Check every detail on it. Verify your name, photo, signature, exam centre, papers and group. If anything is wrong, contact ICAI immediately, because corrections take time.

Know the dates and timings. Group I is on November 2, 4 and 6, and Group II is on November 9, 11 and 13. Papers 1 to 5 run from 2 PM to 5 PM, and Paper 6 from 2 PM to 6 PM. Reach the centre well before the reporting time on the admit card.

If the admit card doesn’t show, check your eligibility. Eligibility holds, such as articleship status updates (due by October 10), can stop it from appearing. Resolve these with ICAI and keep checking icai.org for official notices.

content.text: Students can download the latest Class 11 Biology syllabus from the official CBSE Academic website.

items: Visit cbseacademic.nic.in.
Open the Curriculum 2026-27 section.

sections.heading: How to Prepare for CBSE Class 11 Biology Examination 2026-27?

content.text: Students can plan their Biology preparation using the official chapter list and marks distribution.

items: Complete all 19 chapters prescribed in the Class XI theory syllabus.
Give sufficient revision time to Human Physiology, which carries 18 marks.
Study biological classification, cell structures and plant physiology using the prescribed NCERT textbook.
Practise biological diagrams and explanations relevant to the syllabus.
Review the topics specifically excluded from summative assessment.
Keep the practical record and project work up to date.
Prepare for experiments, slide identification, spotting and viva voce.
Use the official CBSE syllabus PDF to check the scope of each chapter.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Marks split: Biology is assessed out of 100 marks, with 70 for theory and 30 for practical. The subject code is 044.

Unit-wise weightage: Diversity of Living Organisms carries 15 marks, Structural Organisation 10, Cell: Structure and Function 15, Plant Physiology 12 and Human Physiology 18. Human Physiology is the heaviest unit.

Practical (30 marks): This covers a major experiment (5), a minor experiment (4), slide preparation (5), spotting (7), practical record and viva (4) and project work (5). Keep your records and project file complete before the practical.

Question types: The paper is described as roughly 20% MCQ or assertion-reason, 20% case-based or competency-based, and 60% short and long answer questions with compulsory diagrams. One source lists a section-wise pattern totalling 80 marks, which doesn’t match the 70-mark theory paper, so rely on your school’s sample paper.

Dates and chapters: I found no official Class 11 Biology exam date, since your school conducts Class 11 exams. Some sources say the syllabus has 19 chapters while another says 22 chapters. Check the official CBSE syllabus PDF and your school’s notices for the final chapter list and date.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Admission is by Class 12 merit only. There is no entrance exam. Admission is based on Class 12 merit through centralised counselling. Pt. B.D. Sharma University of Health Sciences, Rohtak, conducts the combined online counselling.

Only registered candidates are on the list. Admission is made through online centralised counselling from the list of registered candidates, as per merit in the qualifying exam. If you missed the October 26 to 28 registration window, you won’t appear in Round 1.

Check your name, marks and category. In case of a tie in marks, a tie-breaking rule applies. Check that the marks, category and the 5% relaxation for GNM are right if you claim them. SC, SC (Deprived), BC-A, BC-B and PwBD candidates get a 5% relaxation in merit for GNM.

Fill choices carefully and on time. Choice filling opens before the merit list is out, so fill your preferences carefully and on time. Seats are allotted by merit and your choices, so lock them before the deadline. Check the seat split before you choose. All government institution seats are State Quota, while private institutions offer 50% State Quota and 50% Management Quota. Also, a candidate who is found ineligible or who gives false information can be debarred for three years. Keep your documents ready for verification.

sections.heading: Important Rules for Haryana NEET UG Round 3 Counselling 2026

items: Round 1 or Round 2 candidates who did not get a seat do not need to register again.

content.text: Students can follow the steps below to check the HP Board Class 10 final merit list when the relevant PDF is available on the official website.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Check the merit list on the official site. Use hpbose.org, as the board publishes the merit list there with topper names, marks, ranks and percentages. The top-ranked student is Anmol from Kangra, who scored 699 out of 700, or 99.86%. The overall pass percentage was 83.87%.

Ranks are shared, so ties are normal. Abhinav Mehta, Roohani Damini and Purnima Sharma jointly took second rank at 99.71%. Sources list the names and schools slightly differently, so confirm details against the board’s own list.

Treat the online marksheet as provisional. Students can view provisional mark sheets with their roll number on hpbose.org. You can also get the marksheet through DigiLocker or the UMANG app, but keep the original for admissions.

The re-evaluation window is closed. One source puts the re-evaluation and re-checking application window at May 10 to 25, 2026. Don’t rely on that, because I didn’t see an official HPBOSE notice for it. Improvement exams count towards later merit. One source says a second opportunity examination was set for June 2026 for students wishing to improve their scores, and its results are considered for the final merit list and Class 11 admission. If you’re considering this for a future cycle, check the board’s current notices first.

sections.heading: HPBOSE D.El.Ed Counselling 2026: Seat-Allotment Procedure

content.text: As per the official prospectus, counselling works as follows:

items: HPBOSE prepares a merit list based purely on total marks scored in the CET (no interview is conducted).
Candidates are called for counselling strictly in order of merit, category-wise, as per the reservation roster.
The date, time and venue for each counselling round is announced only on the official HPBOSE website - no individual letters, faxes or phone calls are sent to candidates.
At counselling, eligibility is finally verified against original documents.

Seats are allotted according to the candidate's stated institution preference and the seats available at that candidate's turn. This preference can be exercised only once - once a seat is accepted, it is final, and the candidate cannot request a change of institution.
A candidate who accepts a seat in one round cannot participate in later rounds for re-allotment.
Unfilled or vacated seats are carried forward to the next round strictly by merit.
There is no migration allowed between institutions after admission - neither between DIETs nor between private colleges.

sections.heading: How to Apply / Register for HPBOSE D.El.Ed CET and Counselling

items: Visit the official HPBOSE website: hpbose.org.
Click on the "CET / Vacancy" section, then select the D.El.Ed (CET) 2026 link.
Register and fill in personal, educational, category and exam-centre preference details in capital letters exactly as per your Matriculation certificate.
Upload a scanned photograph (JPG, under 20 KB, 3.5 cm x 4.5 cm) and signature (JPG, under 15 KB, 3.5 cm x 1.5 cm).
Pay the application fee online via net banking, debit card or credit card.
Submit the declaration and download/print the confirmation page for your records.
After the result and merit list are announced, regularly check hpbose.org for your counselling call - no separate communication is sent by post or courier.
Attend counselling in person on the notified date with all original documents, and exercise your institution preference to get your seat allotted.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: The information provided in the online application (name, date of birth, category, etc.) is treated as final and generally cannot be changed once the correction window closes.
No separate letter, fax, email or phone call is sent for any round of counselling - candidates must track hpbose.org themselves.
There is no job guarantee from the Government of Himachal Pradesh after completing the D.El.Ed course.
Attendance requirement during the two-year course is 90%, with a 50% relaxation available for pregnancy/maternity cases on the Principal DIET's recommendation.
All seats are reserved for bonafide residents of Himachal Pradesh.
Any dispute regarding the CET or counselling falls under the jurisdiction of Dharamshala courts.

sections.heading: What Is the HP D.El.Ed CET 2026 Answer Key?

content.text: This section explains what the answer key document actually contains and why it matters for candidates before the final result is prepared.

The HP D.El.Ed CET answer key is a provisional list of correct answers, released by HPBOSE, that candidates can use to estimate their probable score before the official result is declared. sections.heading: How to Raise an Objection Against the HP DElEd CET Answer Key 2026

content.text: This section explains the process, required documents, and deadline for candidates who want to challenge any answer in the provisional key.

Candidates who wish to dispute an answer must submit their objection, along with documentary proof, to the Section Officer at the Question Paper Setting Branch by July 11, 2026. Objections can be sent via email or submitted in person at the HPBOSE board office on any working day. Here is the step-by-step process:

items: Identify the specific question number and the answer you want to challenge in the provisional answer key.
Prepare authentic supporting evidence reference books, standard textbooks, or other credible documentary proof.
Write out the objection details in the prescribed format.
Make sure the email includes your name, roll number, question number, and the supporting evidence.
Objections received after July 11, 2026, will not be considered under any circumstances.

content.text: Alternatively, candidates who prefer not to email their objection can submit it in person at the HPBOSE board office on any working day before the deadline.

sections.heading: What Happens After the Objection Window Closes?

content.text: This section explains how HPBOSE processes challenges and what candidates can expect next in the admission timeline.

Once the objection window closes, subject-matter experts appointed by HPBOSE will review every objection received. Based on this review, HPBOSE will publish the final answer key, and the result for HP D.El.Ed CET 2026 will be prepared using this final key. Candidates should keep checking hpbose.org for updates on the final answer key and subsequent result declaration.

content.text: Before diving into the detailed steps, here is a quick overview of the most important facts about the HPU Result 2026 release.

sections.heading: How to Check and Download HPU Result 2026 - Step-by-Step Guide

content.text: Accessing the HPU Result 2026 is straightforward. Below is a simple, easy-to-follow guide to help you check your HPU semester result and download your marksheet PDF from the official website.

Step 5: If a PDF opens directly, press Ctrl+F (or Cmd+F on Mac) and type your Roll Number or Name to quickly find your entry.

sections.heading: HPU Date Sheet 2026 Released - What Students Need to Know Right Now

content.text: Himachal Pradesh University (HPU), Shimla, has officially released the examination date sheets for 2026 on its official website, hpuniv.ac.in. Students enrolled in undergraduate (UG) programmes such as B.A., B.Sc., and B.Com, as well as various postgraduate (PG) and professional courses, can now access and download the relevant timetables for their upcoming examinations.

Along with the date sheet release, HPU has also issued two critical notifications that every student must read before planning their exam preparation - a withdrawal of datesheets for several PG courses and a paper change notification for M.Sc. Forensic Science students due to the UGC NET examination. Students are strongly advised to check the latest updates directly from the official portal to avoid any confusion.
Visit Official HPU Datesheet Page

links.text: Visit Official HPU Datesheet Page

sections.heading: Key Notifications Released Alongside HPU Date Sheet 2026

content.text: HPU has accompanied the date sheet release with important official notifications. These are not routine updates - they directly affect which students appear for which papers and on which dates.

sections.heading: 1. Withdrawal of Datesheets for PG Courses (Except PG Sciences, B.Tech & B.A. LL.B Honours)

content.text: HPU has officially withdrawn the datesheets for most Postgraduate (PG) courses. The withdrawal notification specifically exempts the following programmes, whose schedules remain valid:

items: PG Sciences (including Mathematics)
B.Tech
B.A. LL.B (Honours)

content.text: Students pursuing other PG programmes - such as M.A., M.Com, and similar humanities or commerce-based postgraduate courses - should note that their previously released datesheets stand withdrawn. Revised datesheets for these courses are expected to be released by HPU separately. Students must not make any exam preparation plans based on the withdrawn schedules and should monitor the official HPU website for updated information.

sections.heading: 2. Change in Papers for M.Sc. Forensic Science Due to UGC NET Examination

content.text: HPU has issued a separate notification specifically for M.Sc. Forensic Science students regarding a change in examination papers. This change has been necessitated by a clash or overlap with the UGC NET Examination schedule, which affects the original date sheet.

Students enrolled in the M.Sc. Forensic Science programme must download and read this notification carefully. The affected paper(s) have been rescheduled to avoid a conflict with the NET exam, ensuring that students who are also NET aspirants are not put in a position where they must choose between the two.
Action Required: M.Sc. Forensic Science students should download the revised notification from the official HPU website and cross-verify their individual exam schedule.

sections.heading: HPU Date Sheet 2026 - UG Annual Examination Schedule Overview

content.text: Himachal Pradesh University conducts undergraduate examinations under the Annual System for traditional UG courses. Here is a summary of the current examination framework based on officially available information:

HPU typically conducts exams in two shifts: a morning shift from 9:00 AM to 12:00 Noon and an afternoon shift from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM. Students must check their individual subject schedules for shift timings, as papers are distributed across both slots.

sections.heading: HPU Date Sheet 2026 - Postgraduate (PG) Examination Overview

content.text: For postgraduate courses, HPU follows the Semester System. PG even semester examinations (2nd and 4th Semester) are generally held in June-July, while odd semester examinations (1st and 3rd Semester) are held in November-December. Students in PG Sciences, B.Tech, and B.A. LL.B (Honours) must check their current date sheets as those schedules remain in effect.

Note: As per the latest notification, datesheets for most other PG courses (except those mentioned above) have been withdrawn and will be reissued. Students are advised to wait for the revised schedule before finalizing their preparation timetable.

sections.heading: How to Download HPU Date Sheet 2026 PDF

content.text: Accessing the HPU exam schedule is straightforward through the university's official website. Follow these steps:

items: Visit the official HPU website: www.hpuniv.ac.in
Click on the "Examinations" tab on the top navigation menu.
Select "Date Sheet" from the dropdown menu.
Browse the list of available date sheets and locate your programme (e.g., UG Annual, PG Semester).
Click the relevant link to open the PDF.
Download and save the date sheet PDF to your device.

content.text: Pro Tip: Always download the date sheet from the official HPU portal and not from third-party websites to ensure you have the most accurate and up-to-date version.

sections.heading: Important Tips for Students Appearing in HPU 2026 Examinations

content.text: Being well-prepared goes beyond knowing your exam dates. Here are a few things every HPU student should keep in mind:

items: Verify your date sheet. Given the recent withdrawal and revision of PG datesheets, always check for updates on the official portal at hpuniv.ac.in before finalising your study schedule.
Download your admit card (roll number slip). HPU releases hall tickets through its student portal. Make sure your photograph and signature are clearly visible on the admit card.
Check your examination centre. HPU sometimes reassigns examination centres based on the number of students enrolled. Verify your centre through the official notification before your exam date.

Report any paper clashes immediately. If two papers in your combination are scheduled at the same time, report it to the Controller of Examinations (COE) through the HPU helpdesk or grievance portal within 7 days of the date sheet release.
M.Sc. Forensic Science students: Download and review the revised paper schedule that was issued due to the UGC NET conflict before preparing your timetable.

detail.title: What Is HPCET 2026 Counselling?
detail.short_info: HPCET 2026 counselling registration is live at himtu.ac.in. Check direct registration link, counselling fee, required documents, seat allotment process, and round-wise schedule here.

content.text: Himachal Pradesh Technical University (HPTU) has opened the counselling registration window for HPCET 2026. Candidates who qualified the Himachal Pradesh Common Entrance Test can now register online at himtu.ac.in to begin the seat allotment process for admission to engineering, pharmacy, and other technical programmes across the state's participating institutes.

This article covers everything candidates need to complete HPCET 2026 counselling registration: the direct application link, step-by-step registration process, counselling fee structure, required documents, eligible courses, and the seat allotment procedure.
Click Here: HPCET 2026 Counselling Registration Begins

links.text: HPCET 2026 Counselling Registration Begins

sections.heading: What Is HPCET 2026 Counselling?

content.text: This section explains the basic purpose of HPCET counselling for readers who are new to the process.

HPCET counselling is the centralised admission process conducted by HPTU, Hamirpur, for candidates who have qualified the Himachal Pradesh Common Entrance Test. Through this process, qualified candidates register online, fill their course and college preferences, and get seats allotted based on their rank, category, and seat availability. The counselling applies to admissions across HPTU's affiliated government and private institutes in Himachal Pradesh.

sections.heading: HPCET 2026 Counselling Registration - Key Highlights

content.text: This section gives a quick overview of the counselling registration status for fast reference.

rows: Candidates who qualified HPCET 2026 or are applying via JEE Main 2026 / qualifying exam scores
B.Tech, B.Pharmacy, B.Pharmacy (Ayurveda), MCA, MBA, MBA (T&HM), B.Sc., and other HPTU-affiliated programmes
50% seats via HPCET rank, 50% via JEE Main score

sections.heading: How to Register for HPCET 2026 Counselling Online

content.text: This section walks candidates through the step-by-step process to complete counselling registration at himtu.ac.in.
Candidates can complete HPCET 2026 counselling registration by following these steps:

items: Visit the official HPTU website, himtu.ac.in.
Click on the HPCET 2026 counselling registration link on the homepage.
Register using basic details such as name, HPCET roll number, and contact information to generate login credentials.
Log in using the registration number and password/date of birth.
Fill in personal, academic, and category details in the counselling-cum-admission form.
Upload the required scanned documents and photograph as per specifications.
Pay the applicable counselling fee through net banking, debit card, or credit card.
Fill course and college preferences in order of priority from the available seat matrix.
Lock your choices before the deadline; unlocked choices may be auto-considered as locked once the window closes.
Submit the form and save/print the confirmation page for future reference.

sections.heading: HPCET 2026 Counselling Fee

content.text: This section details the fee candidates need to pay during registration, based on category.
The counselling fee for candidates who do not already hold an HPCET score is structured by category, as per HPTU's notified fee schedule:

Candidates applying through HPCET alone are generally exempted from this additional fee, while those applying via both HPCET and a national-level test may be required to pay the applicable amount. Fee payment must be completed online through net banking, debit card, or credit card; no other payment mode is accepted.

sections.heading: Documents Required for HPCET 2026 Counselling

content.text: This section lists the documents candidates must keep ready for verification during counselling.
Candidates must upload and later present the following documents in original for verification:

items: HPCET 2026 / JEE Main 2026 / qualifying exam scorecard
Class 10 mark sheet and certificate (for age proof)
Class 12 mark sheet and passing certificate
School leaving certificate / transfer certificate
Category certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS), if applicable
BPL/IRDP certificate, if applicable
Passport-size photograph and signature in the specified format

sections.heading: HPCET 2026 Counselling Process: Step-by-Step Stages

content.text: This section breaks down the complete counselling journey from registration to admission confirmation.
The HPCET 2026 counselling procedure includes the following stages:

items: Online Registration: Candidates register at himtu.ac.in and pay the counselling fee within the notified window.
Choice Filling: Candidates select course and college preferences from the published seat matrix, in order of priority.
Locking of Choices: Preferences must be locked before the deadline; any choices left unlocked may be treated as locked automatically.
Seat Allotment: Seats are allotted based on HPCET 2026 rank, category, preferences submitted, and seat availability.
Document Verification: Allotted candidates upload or present documents for verification.
Admission Fee Payment: Candidates confirm their allotted seat by paying the admission fee.
Reporting to Institute: Candidates report to the allotted institute with original documents within the specified timeline.
Multiple Rounds: HPTU conducts more than one round of counselling including a mop-up or stray vacancy round until seats are filled.

sections.heading: Courses and Institutes Covered Under HPCET 2026 Counselling

content.text: This section explains which programmes and colleges accept admission through HPCET counselling.

HPCET 2026 scores are accepted by HPTU and over 50 affiliated government and private colleges, deemed universities, and other institutes established under the Himachal Pradesh State Act. Admissions are offered for:

items: B.Tech (Bachelor of Technology)
B.Pharmacy and B.Pharmacy (Ayurveda)
B.Sc.
MCA (Master of Computer Applications)
MBA and MBA (Tourism & Hospitality Management)
M.Tech and other postgraduate technical programmes

content.text: For B.Tech admissions specifically, 50% of seats at HPTU-affiliated institutes are filled through HPCET 2026 ranks, while the remaining 50% are filled based on JEE Main 2026 scores.

sections.heading: HP PAT 2026 Merit List & Tie-Breaking Criteria

content.text: The HP PAT 2026 merit list is published alongside the result on hptechboard.com. It ranks all qualified candidates based on their total marks obtained in the entrance examination. Understanding how ties are resolved helps candidates know exactly where they stand.
In cases where two or more candidates score identical marks, the board applies a tie-breaking formula in the following order of priority:

items: Marks in Chemistry - The candidate with higher Chemistry marks ranks higher.
Marks in Physics - If Chemistry marks are also equal, Physics scores are compared.
Marks in Biology/Mathematics - The next tiebreaker if Physics scores are also tied.
Marks in English - Applied if the above three subjects also result in a tie.
Age - In case of a further tie, the older candidate is given the higher rank.

sections.heading: How to Calculate Marks Using HPCET 2026 Answer Key

content.text: Once the tentative answer key is downloaded, candidates can estimate their HPCET 2026 score by applying the marking scheme to their responses. The marking scheme for each paper is given in the official HPCET 2026 information brochure, and candidates must follow that pattern only.
The general process is as follows:

items: Note down the total number of questions and marks per question for your paper as mentioned in the HPCET 2026 exam pattern.
For every correct answer that matches the option given in the answer key, add the full marks allotted per question.
For every wrong answer, deduct marks as per the negative marking specified in the brochure.
No marks are added or deducted for questions which were left unanswered.
After going through all questions, total your marks to get your approximate score in HPCET 2026 for that specific course.

content.text: For example, if a paper carries 100 questions with 2 marks each and 0.5 marks negative per wrong answer, and a candidate gets 70 questions correct and 20 wrong, the estimated score will be: Correct: 70 × 2 = 140 Wrong: 20 × 0.5 = 10 (to be deducted) Estimated score = 140 − 10 = 130
This calculated score is only indicative; the final result will be based on the University’s evaluation and the final answer key.

sections.heading: HPCET 2026 Answer Key Objection Process (Tentative)

content.text: HPTU usually allows candidates to challenge the provisional or tentative answer key, subject to certain conditions, although the exact procedure and dates are confirmed only through official notifications. Candidates are therefore advised to carefully read the instructions provided with the HPCET 2026 answer key notice on the official website.
Typically, the objection process includes the following steps:

items: Objections must be submitted within a specified time window after the release of the tentative answer key.
Candidates have to mention the question number, booklet code, the answer given in the provisional key and the answer they believe is correct, along with supporting proof from authentic sources.
There may be an objection fee per question, which can be refunded if the challenge is found valid, depending on University rules.

content.text: After the objection window is closed, expert committees examine all challenges. Based on their recommendations, HPTU may revise the answers and publish the final answer key. The result is then prepared strictly on the basis of this final key, and further objections are normally not entertained.

sections.heading: HPCET 2026 Exam - Courses, Eligibility & Pattern (Quick Info)

content.text: This section gives users a broader picture and also helps internal linking to your exam overview pages.
HPCET 2026 Courses Offered
HPCET 2026 is conducted for admission to various undergraduate and postgraduate courses offered by Himachal Pradesh Technical University and its affiliated colleges. Major programmes include:

items: Bachelor of Technology (B.Tech)
Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharmacy)

content.text: You can add internal links from each course name to your detailed course or admission pages.
Basic Eligibility for HPCET 2026 (UG & PG)
The detailed eligibility criteria are provided in the HPCET 2026 information brochure, and candidates must strictly verify them before applying. However, in broad terms:

items: For B.Tech and B.Pharmacy: Candidates must have passed 10+2 or equivalent examination from a recognised board with the required combination of subjects and minimum aggregate marks stipulated by HPTU.
For MCA, MBA, MBA (T&HM), M.Sc Physics and M.Sc Environmental Sciences: Candidates should possess a relevant bachelor’s degree with the minimum percentage specified in the prospectus.

content.text: For precise eligibility (including subject combination, age limit and relaxation details), candidates should always refer to the official HPCET 2026 prospectus available on the University website.
HPCET 2026 Exam Pattern & Marking Scheme
HPCET is conducted in offline mode as a pen‑and‑paper OMR based test. The exam pattern varies slightly from course to course, but some common features are:

items: The question paper consists of objective type multiple-choice questions.
The medium of the question paper is generally English.
Each question carries equal marks and there is negative marking for incorrect answers as per the official scheme for that particular programme.

content.text: For course-wise exam pattern, distribution of questions by subject and detailed marking scheme, candidates should check the dedicated “HPCET 2026 Exam Pattern” notification or your separate exam pattern article.

sections.heading: HPCET 2026 Result, Cut Off and Counselling (Next Steps)

content.text: This section satisfies the natural follow-up questions users have after checking the answer key.
HPCET 2026 Result Date (Expected Overview)

After the final answer key is published and the OMR sheets are evaluated, HPTU declares the HPCET 2026 result on its official website. The result link is usually made available in the “Results” or “HPCET” section, where candidates can log in and download their scorecard.

The exact date for the declaration of the HPCET 2026 result will be notified by the University through an official notice. Candidates should regularly visit the website or follow trusted education portals for timely updates.
HPCET 2026 Cut Off and Merit List
Once the results are announced, the University releases course-wise and category-wise cut off marks or merit lists. These cut offs are determined based on several factors, such as:

items: Number of candidates appearing for the exam
Total seats available in a particular course
Difficulty level of the question paper
Previous year cut-off trends and reservation norms

content.text: Candidates securing marks equal to or above the notified cut off will be considered for counselling and further admission processes.
HPCET 2026 Counselling Process (Short Summary)
Eligible candidates who qualify as per the HPCET 2026 cut off must participate in the University’s counselling process. The broad steps in counselling generally include:

items: Online registration for counselling within the stipulated dates
Payment of counselling fee (if any)
Filling and locking choices of courses and colleges
Verification of documents at designated centres or online, as per the procedure
Seat allotment based on merit, preferences and reservation policy

content.text: After seat allotment, candidates must confirm their admission by reporting to the allotted institute within the prescribed time along with original documents and fees.

sections.heading: HP PAT 2026 Application Process

content.text: The HP PAT 2026 application process is completely online. Candidates need to visit the official website, register on the Eakadamik portal, fill in the application form, upload documents, and complete the online fee payment.

sections.heading: How to Apply for HP PAT 2026 Online

content.text: The HP PAT Application Form 2026 can be filled only through the online Eakadamik portal linked from the Board’s website. The process includes new user registration, login, form filling, document upload and online fee payment.

items: Visit the official website: www.hptechboard.com.
Click on “Online Admission-2026”.

Fill in the registration details and submit the form.
Receive login credentials and registration number through SMS/email.
Login to the portal and complete the application form.
Enter personal, category, domicile, address, and academic details.
Upload photograph and signature in the prescribed format.
Accept the terms and conditions and proceed to payment.
Pay the application fee online through debit card, credit card, net banking, or UPI.
After successful payment, download and print the submitted application form.

HP PAT 2026 Exam Pattern

content.text: HP PAT 2026 will be conducted through a single objective-type question paper of 3 hours duration. The paper will include questions from Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, and English.

items: All questions will be objective type.
Each correct answer carries 4 marks.
1 mark will be deducted for each wrong answer.
The exam will be held in OMR format.
Maths, Physics, and Chemistry portions will be available in English and Hindi.

sections.heading: HP PAT 2026 Exam Date

content.text: HP PAT 2026 exam will be conducted on 17 May 2026 (Sunday). The examination timing will be from 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM, and the duration of the paper will be 3 hours.

Roll numbers will be available on the Board website from 11 May 2026 onwards, and candidates must download the admit card online because it will not be sent by post. No candidate will be allowed to appear in the exam without a valid admit card.

detail.title: Ladakh MBBS BDS Admission 2026 - Overview
detail.short_info: Ladakh's Health & Medical Education Department has revised the Central Pool MBBS and BDS admission guidelines for 2026-27, replacing the old category-wise roster with a single NEET merit list.

content.text: The Health & Medical Education (H&ME) Department, Union Territory of Ladakh, issued revised guidelines on September 22, 2026, for admission to MBBS and BDS seats under the Central Pool. The revision replaces the existing category-wise roster system with a single merit list based purely on NEET ranking. The change was made following the creation of seven new districts in Ladakh and was approved by Lieutenant Governor V K Saxena. For the 2026-27 academic session, the Centre has allotted 7 MBBS seats and 2 BDS seats to Ladakh under the Central Pool.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Choose an option when the allotment comes out. In Round 1, KEA warned that candidates who don’t select a choice within the deadline are treated as not interested in the seat and moved to choice-4. Don’t miss the window.

Choice-1 means fee, slip and reporting. Choice-1 candidates must download the seat confirmation slip and report to the allotted college by the stated deadline. Pay the fee online before that, because the allotment is cancelled if you skip any of these steps.

Surrendering a seat may need an in-person visit. For Round 1, KEA required that candidates surrendering a choice 1 or 2 seat do so in person at the KEA office in Bengaluru by a fixed time. Check whether Round 4 uses the same rule.

Later rounds may have fewer choices. In Round 1 candidates had all four choice options available. In later UGCET rounds, KEA said choices 2 and 3 would not be available. NEET Round 4 may be similarly restricted, so read the choice rules in the notice carefully.

Keep your documents and the official schedule at hand. Carry your NEET UG 2026 scorecard and admit card, along with the allotment letter and fee receipt. KEA often extends deadlines, but don’t count on it. Follow only kea.kar.nic.in for dates.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Other State (OS) quota: For General-category OS, Round 1 of 2026 (13 June) closed at rank 1,317, and the final-round 2025 closing rank was 1,449. That makes it one of the toughest NIT CSE seats.

Home State (Tamil Nadu) quota: One report puts the Round 5 closing rank at 4,015 for home state and 1,373 for other state. Round 4 CSE is listed at 1034 to 3812. Home State ranks are much more relaxed than OS ranks.

Check the quota and category: The cutoff differs by quota (HS or OS), category (General, OBC-NCL, SC, ST, EWS) and gender seat type. JoSAA publishes separate opening and closing ranks for each category, so compare yourself against the right row.
Rank and percentile: CSE at OS generally needs a General rank under about 1,500. This is a rough guide, since the final cutoff is only set by the round-wise counselling outcome.

Verify on the official portal: Third-party reporting of final-round figures has been inconsistent, so verify them on the JoSAA OR-CR portal at josaa.nic.in. I couldn’t confirm an official 2026 final-round figure, and some sites mix 2025 and 2026 data.

sections.heading: How to Complete Karnataka PGCET Round 2 Option Entry 2026?

content.text: Eligible candidates can access the KEA PGCET 2026 Centralised Allotment Process portal and submit their course and college preferences online.

items: Visit the KEA PGCET 2026 Option Entry Portal.
Enter the CET number and application number as required.
Complete the OTP and other verification steps displayed on the portal.
Access the option entry facility.
Check the available colleges and courses against the provisional seat matrix.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Download the matrix from the official site only. Use the PGCET 2026 section of the KEA portal. The Round 2 matrix should show only seats left vacant after Round 1, so earlier matrices no longer apply.
The provisional matrix can change. Draft and provisional matrices are for reference, and KEA fixes the final one before allotment. Report any discrepancies within the objection window.
Re-do your option entry. Edit or re-enter your web options against the Round 2 seat matrix. Put the most preferred college and course first, and drop options that were taken in Round 1.

Decide how to treat your Round 1 seat. Confirm whether you want to keep it, upgrade or give it up, because the choice affects your Round 2 eligibility and any fee refund or forfeiture. Check the notice’s rules before you decide.

Keep dates and documents ready. Note the option-entry deadline, the mock and provisional allotment dates, and the fee payment and reporting dates. Keep your original certificates, such as rank card, category and Kannada/rural claims if any, and fee receipts, ready for verification.

How to Apply for CEE Kerala DNB Post MBBS 2026?

content.text: CEE Kerala has specified five mandatory application steps.

items: Visit the official DNB Post MBBS 2026 application portal.
Click Registration and enter the required mobile number and email address.
Create a password and save the system-generated application number.
Log in using the application number and password.
Complete the application form with personal, educational, NEET PG and applicable Government service details.
Pay the prescribed application fee of Rs. 1,000 plus gateway charges.
Upload the required images and certificates.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Eligibility is limited. All the State quota seats are earmarked for In-Service candidates (Medical Education, Health Service or Insurance Medical Service of the Govt. of Kerala), and you must hold an MBBS degree.

Apply online only, on the CEE website. The 2025 round let candidates apply online through the CEE website until 06.11.2025, 12.00 PM. The 2026 deadline will be in the new notification, and no late submissions are accepted.
The fee is Rs 1,000, paid online. In earlier rounds, it was non-refundable. The 2026 Post Diploma notice says payment is by credit card, debit card or net banking.

Upload your documents with the application. After paying, you must upload your photo, signature and the required certificates, such as proof of nativity. Nothing can be submitted after the last date, so have all of it scanned in advance.

Register your options and skip the printout. You must select and order your options (speciality and institution combinations) as part of the online application, and the application is complete only after options are registered. There is no need to send a printout of the acknowledgement page or any documents to the CEE office. Still, save the acknowledgement page for your records.

sections.heading: How to Complete Kerala PG Dental Admission 2026 Option Entry?

content.text: The earlier Round 3 option registration window ended on 12 October 2026. The following steps explain the procedure prescribed in the official notification for that window.

items: Visit the official website at cee.kerala.gov.in.
Open the PG Dental 2026 Candidate Portal.
Enter the application number and password to log in.
Select the Option Registration menu.
Choose the preferred MDS courses and dental colleges.
Arrange the options according to admission preference.
Pay the applicable option registration fee.
Complete the option registration process within the prescribed deadline.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Check the deadline first. Log in to the “PG Dental 2026 - Candidate Portal” with your application number and password, then open “Option Registration”. Confirm the current closing date and time on the CEE notification, because deadlines are often extended.

Fresh options need a fresh fee. Fresh option registration is available in the third (final) round, but with a fresh option registration fee. Earlier-round fees are forfeited if you were allotted a seat in Round 2 and did not report, did not join, or quit after joining.

Fill options in strict order of preference. Choose course and college combinations carefully. Allotment follows your rank, category and the order of your list, so put your most-wanted choices first and don’t add colleges you wouldn’t join.
Save and confirm your list. Unconfirmed or unsaved options may not be considered. Take a printout or screenshot of the final list.

Prepare to join if allotted. Download the allotment memo, pay the fee or balance fee, and report to the college within the joining dates. Keep your original documents ready, including your Kerala State Dental Council registration, as admission requires the original.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG Round 1 Seat Allotment Result 2026 Released

content.text: The Directorate of Medical Education, Madhya Pradesh, has announced the first-round provisional seat allotment result for NEET PG 2026 counselling. The result was released on 29 October 2026 for candidates who completed the required registration and choice filling procedures.
The allotment has been prepared based on candidates' state merit positions, submitted college and course preferences, applicable reservation categories and available postgraduate medical seats.

Candidates can check the published allotment list to identify their allotted institution, postgraduate course and relevant seat category. The result is provisional, and admission remains subject to verification of documents and completion of the prescribed formalities.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG Counselling 2026 Round 1 Important Dates

content.text: DME Madhya Pradesh has announced the Round 1 result and the subsequent reporting, upgradation and resignation schedule. Candidates should carefully note that the reporting and upgradation deadlines have different closing times.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG Counselling 2026 Round 1 Result Download Link

content.text: Candidates can access the Round 1 provisional allotment list through the official DME MPOnline counselling website. The allotment list is published in PDF format, while individual provisional allotment letters are available through candidate login.

rows: Round 1 Opening and Closing Rank PDF

content.text: The two direct PDF addresses above were publicly shared as official-domain result links but could not be independently opened during verification. Candidates should use the main counselling portal if either direct link is unavailable.

sections.heading: How to Download MP NEET PG Round 1 Result 2026?

content.text: Candidates can follow these steps to check the MP NEET PG 2026 Round 1 provisional seat allotment result.

items: Visit the official counselling portal at dme.mponline.gov.in.
Open the PG Medical Counselling section for MD/MS admissions.
Find the First Round Allotment List for MP State Combined NEET PG Counselling 2026.
Open the provisional allotment result PDF.
Use the PDF search option to find the candidate's NEET PG roll number or name.
Check the allotted college, course and applicable seat category.
Download the PDF for future reference.
Log in to the candidate account to download the individual provisional allotment letter if a seat has been allotted.

content.text: The individual allotment letter is required for the subsequent admission process. Candidates should not rely only on a screenshot or the general allotment list when reporting to their allotted institution.

sections.heading: Details to Check in MP NEET PG Round 1 Allotment List 2026

content.text: The Round 1 allotment list provides information about candidates and the postgraduate medical seats allotted through state counselling.
Candidates should check the following details, wherever shown in the official result document:

items: Candidate's Name
NEET PG Roll Number
State Common Merit Rank
NEET PG All India Rank
Candidate Category
Allotted Medical College
Allotted Course and Speciality
Allotted Seat Category or Quota

content.text: Candidates should verify that their allotted course and institution match the information in their individual allotment letter. Any discrepancy should be through the official counselling or allotted college authorities.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG 2026 Provisional Allotment Letter

content.text: Candidates who have received a seat in the first round must download their provisional allotment letters through the official DME MPOnline candidate login.

The allotment letter contains the admission details required for reporting to the allotted medical institution. It must be presented along with the applicable original documents during the verification process.

Downloading the allotment letter does not by itself complete the admission process. Candidates must satisfy the document verification, fee payment and reporting requirements within the prescribed schedule.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG Round 1 Reporting Dates 2026

content.text: Physical reporting and admission at allotted medical colleges will take place between 30 October and 10 November 2026, up to 6:00 PM.
Candidates who have been allotted a postgraduate medical seat must report in person to their respective institutions for the prescribed verification and admission procedures.

rows: Document Verification, Fee Payment and Admission

content.text: The allotted institution will verify the candidate's eligibility and original academic records. Candidates should follow the official admission instructions and confirm the applicable tuition fees with their allotted colleges.

sections.heading: Documents Required for MP NEET PG Counselling 2026 Round 1 Reporting

content.text: According to the admission instructions, allotted candidates must carry their original documents along with two sets of self-attested photocopies for verification.

items: MP NEET PG 2026 Provisional Allotment Letter
NEET PG 2026 Admit Card
NEET PG 2026 Scorecard or Rank Letter
MBBS Degree Certificate or Provisional Passing Certificate
MBBS Mark Sheets of All Professional Examinations
Compulsory Rotatory Internship Completion Certificate
Permanent or Provisional Medical Registration Certificate
Valid Government Photo Identity Proof
Madhya Pradesh Domicile Certificate, if applicable
SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwD Certificate, if applicable
In-Service Experience or Sponsorship Certificate, if applicable

content.text: Candidates should verify the complete document requirements with their allotted college and the latest official counselling instructions before reporting.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG Round 2 Upgradation 2026

content.text: DME Madhya Pradesh has provided an option for eligible Round 1 allotted candidates to express willingness for upgradation in Round 2.
The upgradation willingness window is scheduled from 30 October to 10 November 2026, closing at 11:59 PM.

Candidates considering upgradation should review the official counselling rules before submitting their willingness. The implications for retaining or changing the Round 1 allotted seat are governed by the applicable counselling instructions.
The detailed Round 2 choice filling and seat allotment dates were not provided in the supplied Round 1 result announcement.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG Round 1 Resignation and Admission Cancellation 2026

content.text: Candidates who wish to resign from or cancel a Round 1 admission can use the prescribed online resignation or admission cancellation process.

Candidates should carefully review the official admission and resignation rules before taking any action. The consequences of cancellation and eligibility for later counselling rounds depend on the applicable DME regulations.

sections.heading: MP NEET PG 2026 Round 1 Opening and Closing Rank

content.text: In addition to the provisional allotment list, an opening and closing rank document for the first round has been publicly linked on the DME MPOnline domain.
The document is intended to provide course-wise and college-wise allotment rank information. Candidates may use it to understand the ranks at which seats were allotted in the first round.
These opening and closing ranks describe completed Round 1 allotments. They should not be treated as guaranteed admission thresholds for subsequent counselling rounds.

items: The Round 1 provisional seat allotment result was released on 29 October 2026.
Allotted candidates must download their individual provisional allotment letters.
Physical reporting begins on 30 October 2026.
The reporting and document verification deadline is 10 November 2026 at 6:00 PM.
Candidates must carry the required original documents and photocopies.
Applicable admission and tuition fees must be paid according to the allotted college's instructions.
Willingness for Round 2 upgradation can be submitted until 10 November 2026 at 11:59 PM.
The resignation and admission cancellation deadline is 10 November 2026 at 6:00 PM.
