sections.heading: How to Correct Errors in MP Board Dummy Admit Card 2027?

items: Download or obtain the MPBSE Dummy Admit Card 2027.
Check the personal and examination details against school records.
Identify any incorrect or missing information.
Inform the school principal or authorised school staff.
Provide the relevant details or supporting documents requested by the school.
Ask the school to complete the correction through the prescribed MPBSE process.
Verify the corrected information once it is available.

sections.heading: MPBSE Class 10th and 12th Exam Dates 2027

content.text: The Madhya Pradesh Board of Secondary Education has published the annual main examination timetable for 2027. Class 12 examinations will begin on 17 February 2027, followed by Class 10 examinations on 24 February 2027.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Check every detail on the dummy card. A dummy admit card is a draft for correcting errors before the final one is issued. Verify your name, parents’ names, date of birth, photo, signature, subjects and medium. Don’t treat it as the exam ticket.

Get corrections made through your school. In the 2025 case before the High Court, the board’s dummy admit card was issued and then the school’s documents were scrutinised. Errors are usually fixed by the school or principal, not by individual students. Tell your school quickly and keep proof of what you reported.
Mind the correction deadline. I don’t have the 2027 deadline yet. Last time the correction window was short, so don’t wait. Once the final admit card is issued, changes are much harder.

Don’t treat the dummy card as the final one. The admit card is released later at the board’s website. Check what the board says at release, since the portal name has varied (mpbse.nic.in and mpbse.mponline.gov.in).

Note the exam-day timings. Theory exams run from 9 am to noon. Students must reach their centres by 8 am and be seated by 8.30 am, with entry closing at 8.45 am. Question papers are given out at 8.45 am.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria for Nagaland University UG Admission 2026

content.text: Before applying, candidates should understand how selection works, since Nagaland University does not rely on Class XII marks alone.

Admissions will be granted strictly on merit based on candidates' CUET-UG scores and Class XII examination performance, as per the eligibility criteria prescribed by the respective academic departments. This means:

items: Candidates must have appeared for CUET-UG 2026 in the relevant subject combination.
Final merit is a combination of the CUET-UG score and Class XII marks.
Department-specific eligibility norms (such as required subjects in Class XII) apply, so applicants should check the specific requirements for their chosen discipline on the official portal.

sections.heading: Nagaland University UG Admission 2026: Important Dates

content.text: Timing matters a great deal in this admission cycle, as the entire process from application to final seat allotment runs on a tight schedule. The section below lays out every key date candidates need to track.

Applications are open till 15th July 2026 for FYUGP B.Sc. Honours and Honours with Research programmes. The University will publish the list of shortlisted candidates on 16th July 2026, while admissions for selected candidates will be conducted from 17th July to 20th July 2026. Admissions from the waiting list are scheduled from 21st July to 23rd July 2026.
Candidates are advised to keep checking the official admission portal regularly, as revised or extended dates (if any) are typically notified there first.

sections.heading: How to Apply for Nagaland University FYUGP Admission 2026

content.text: Applicants naturally want a simple, step-by-step way to submit their application without missing any part of the process. Here's how it works.
Interested candidates can submit their applications through the University's admission portal at admission.nagalanduniversity.ac.in. The general process is as follows:

items: Visit the official admission portal: admission.nagalanduniversity.ac.in
Register with basic personal details to create a login.
Log in and select the FYUGP B.Sc. Honours/Honours with Research programme.
Choose your preferred discipline (Botany, Chemistry, Mathematics, Physics, or Zoology).
Fill in academic details, including Class X and Class XII information and CUET-UG scorecard details.
Upload the required documents (see checklist below).
Review the form carefully before final submission, as incomplete or incorrect forms may be rejected.
Submit the application within the deadline of 15th July 2026.

content.text: Krishanth Abhinav M topped the Union Territory of Puducherry in the Re-NEET UG 2026 result, securing All India Rank (AIR) 553 with a percentile of 99.9721, as reported by exam-tracking sources including Aakash Institute and Daily Jagran.

sections.heading: CENTAC Merit List 2026 - Draft UG Non-NEET Merit List Released

content.text: The Centralised Admission Committee (CENTAC), under the Directorate of Higher and Technical Education, Government of Puducherry, has released the draft merit list for UG Non-NEET admissions 2026-2027 on 17 June 2026. The list covers a wide range of undergraduate courses across colleges in the Union Territory of Puducherry, including Arts, Law, Agriculture & Horticulture, Biology-based courses, B.Tech, B.Pharm, Nursing, and Diploma programmes. Candidates can check their category-wise rank and submit objections, if any, through the official CENTAC dashboard before the deadline.
Click Here: CENTAC Merit List 2026

links.text: CENTAC Merit List 2026

sections.heading: What Is the CENTAC Draft Merit List 2026?

content.text: This section explains what the draft merit list is and why it matters to applicants.

The draft merit list is a preliminary ranking of candidates who applied for UG Non-NEET admission through CENTAC for the academic year 2026-2027. It is published before the final merit list so that candidates get an opportunity to verify their rank and details, and raise objections if there are discrepancies. The list has been published separately for each course and is further broken down by category: Overall, Puducherry (local), Other States, and NRI/NRI SP/OCI/FN (foreign nationals and related categories).

sections.heading: CENTAC Merit List 2026 - Key Dates

content.text: This section lists the important dates candidates need to know regarding the draft merit list and objection window.
Candidates who find any error in their rank, marks, or category in the draft list must raise an objection within this window, as no requests are typically considered after the deadline closes.

sections.heading: How to Submit Objections to the CENTAC Draft Merit List

content.text: This section explains the step-by-step process to raise an objection against the draft merit list.
If a candidate notices any discrepancy in the draft merit list, they can raise it directly through the CENTAC online portal. The process is as follows:

items: Visit the official CENTAC UG Degree admission portal.
Log in to your candidate dashboard using your registered credentials.
Locate the objection or grievance section on the dashboard.
Enter the details of the discrepancy you have identified.
Submit the objection before 20 June 2026, 11:00 AM.

content.text: Candidates should keep supporting documents ready in case they are asked to substantiate their objection.

sections.heading: Important Notes on Specific Courses

content.text: This section highlights special conditions that apply to certain courses in the merit list.
A few courses have additional conditions candidates should be aware of:

items: B.Sc. Nursing (Government Quota): The merit list will be published only after the Puducherry Nursing Entrance Test (PNET) 2026 result is declared.
B.Sc. Nursing (Self-Supporting Quota): This list depends on the UG-NEET 2026 result and will be released after that result is announced.
B.Tech. (Other State, based on H.Sc. Marks): This merit list will be operated only after the JEE-based merit list for the same category has been exhausted.
Ward of Farmer and Village Extension Worker categories: No candidates are listed (NIL) under these categories at present.
PWD and MSP categories: Lists for Persons with Disabilities and Meritorious Sports Persons are yet to be published.

sections.heading: How to Check Your CENTAC Merit List Rank

content.text: This section explains how candidates can view their rank in the draft merit list.
Candidates can check their rank in the draft merit list by following these steps:

items: Go to the official CENTAC website (centacpuducherry.in).
Open the UG Non-NEET 2026-2027 draft merit list page.
Select the relevant course and category (Overall, Puducherry, Other States, or NRI/OCI/FN).
Click on "View" against the corresponding course to open the list.
Use your application/roll number to locate your rank within the document.

sections.heading: Why the Draft Merit List Matters Before Final Counselling

content.text: This section explains the purpose of releasing a draft list before the final merit list and counselling process.

Publishing a draft list before finalising admissions ensures transparency and fairness in the selection process. It gives every applicant a chance to verify their marks, category, and rank, and to flag any clerical or technical errors before they affect final seat allotment. Once objections are reviewed, CENTAC will release the final merit list, which will then be used for the counselling and seat allotment process for UG Non-NEET admissions 2026-2027 in Puducherry colleges.

content.text: BFUHS Punjab B.Sc Nursing Round 3 Seat Matrix 2026 will be released by Baba Farid University of Health Sciences (BFUHS), Faridkot on September 22, 2026. The seat matrix will show the vacant seats available across colleges for Round 3 of B.Sc Nursing counselling. Candidates who want to surrender seats allotted in Round 1 or Round 2 can do so at their respective colleges by September 21, 2026. The last date to fill Round 3 choices is September 23, 2026.

sections.heading: BFUHS Punjab B.Sc Nursing 2026 - Quick Overview

rows: Baba Farid University of Health Sciences (BFUHS), Faridkot

sections.heading: BFUHS Punjab B.Sc Nursing Round 3 Seat Matrix 2026 - Important Dates

content.text: Candidates preparing for Round 3 counselling should keep the following dates in mind:

items: September 21, 2026: Last date for Round 1/Round 2 admitted candidates to surrender their seats at the respective college.
September 22, 2026: BFUHS Punjab B.Sc Nursing Round 3 seat matrix release date.
September 23, 2026: Last date to submit Round 3 choices/preferences online.

sections.heading: How to Fill BFUHS Round 3 Choices

content.text: While the complete step-by-step choice-filling process was not detailed in the official notification, candidates are generally expected to:

items: Visit the official BFUHS admission portal, admission.bfuhsonline.ac.in.
Log in using their PPMET 2026 counselling credentials.
Refer to the released Round 3 seat matrix PDF for available colleges, categories, and quotas.
Arrange and submit college, category, and quota preferences in order of priority.
Submit choices before the last date, September 23, 2026.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Review the Round 3 seat matrix carefully for preferred colleges, categories, and quotas before entering choices.

Do not restrict choices only to seats listed in the matrix. BFUHS has previously stated that candidates may submit preferences for colleges even when a particular seat is not reflected in the tentative vacancy position.
Arrange college, category, and quota preferences carefully before final submission.
A candidate already holding a seat from Round 1 or Round 2 may participate in Round 3 if eligible for upgradation. Such movement can create fresh vacancies at other colleges.
Candidates who receive a Round 3 allotment should be prepared for document verification, eligibility checking, medical formalities, and fee payment within the prescribed timeline.

A vacancy shown under one category or quota does not automatically mean the same seat is available under another category. Candidates should verify the exact classification before submitting preferences.

rows: Verifying that every answer has been evaluated, marks are correctly totalled and carried forward to the main sheet, and no question has been left unchecked. The actual answers are not re-assessed.

items: PSEB re-checks or re-evaluates the answer script as per the option chosen.

detail.short_info: Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) has revised the VITEEE 2027 examination pattern for B.Tech admissions. content.text: VITEEE 2027 Exam Pattern Revised: Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) has reduced the B.Tech entrance examination duration from 2 hours 30 minutes to 2 hours (120 minutes). The revised examination will contain 100 multiple-choice questions carrying 400 marks. VIT has introduced fixed sectional timers, with 50 minutes for Mathematics/Biology, 30 minutes each for Physics and Chemistry, and 10 minutes for English and Aptitude combined.

Candidates will receive four marks for each correct answer, while one mark will be deducted for every incorrect response. The computer-based examination is tentatively scheduled from 27 April to 2 May 2027. Registration is open at viteee.vit.ac.in until 31 March 2027.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Revised Exam Pattern Overview
VITEEE 2027 Exam Pattern Revised: What Has Changed?

content.text: VIT has introduced several changes to the examination structure for the 2027 admission cycle. The important revisions concern overall duration, total questions, marks and time management.

The comparison describes the previous examination format and the new 2027 structure. Candidates preparing for VITEEE 2027 should follow the latest official pattern instead of relying on older mock tests or preparation guides.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Subject-Wise Exam Pattern and Marks Distribution

content.text: The revised question paper has five subjects but four timed sections, because English and Aptitude share one ten-minute block.
Mathematics or Biology carries the highest weightage, contributing 160 of the total 400 marks. Physics and Chemistry carry 100 marks each, while English and Aptitude together carry 40 marks.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Sectional Timers Explained

content.text: One of the most important changes in VITEEE 2027 is the introduction of fixed sectional time limits.
Each subject block has a defined duration. Candidates must attempt the questions within the available time instead of freely distributing the full 120 minutes across the entire paper.
The published examination update states that responses are saved and locked when a sectional timer expires, preventing candidates from returning to earlier questions after the section closes.

The official VIT website independently confirms the fixed time allocation for each block. Candidates should follow the instructions displayed during the examination for the precise navigation and section-locking procedure.

sections.heading: Can Candidates Return to Previous Sections in VITEEE 2027?

content.text: According to the published revised-pattern explanation, candidates cannot revisit a completed section after its allotted time expires.
This means students should carefully review their attempted answers while the relevant section remains active.

VIT's official portal confirms the use of sectional timers. However, the full computer-based test navigation rules should be checked through the official examination instructions and mock test once available.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Mathematics and Biology Section

content.text: The Mathematics or Biology section contains 40 multiple-choice questions worth 160 marks.
Candidates receive 50 minutes to complete this section, making it the largest and longest timed block in the examination.
Candidates should select the correct MPCEA or BPCEA examination stream according to their Class 12 subjects and intended B.Tech programmes.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Physics and Chemistry Exam Pattern

content.text: Physics and Chemistry each contain 25 multiple-choice questions.
Each subject carries 100 marks and has a separate 30-minute sectional timer.
The average available time is approximately 72 seconds per question in each of these sections.
Students should practise calculations and concept-based questions under timed conditions to become familiar with the revised format.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 English and Aptitude Section

content.text: The combined English and Aptitude section carries ten questions and 40 marks.
Important: VIT provides only ten minutes for English and Aptitude together. The university does not list separate ten-minute timers for each subject.
Candidates should practise both sections together within a single ten-minute limit.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 Negative Marking and Marking Scheme

content.text: VITEEE 2027 has negative marking for incorrect answers under its revised examination pattern.
For example, a candidate answering 60 questions correctly and 20 incorrectly, while leaving the remaining 20 unanswered, would receive 220 marks.
The score is calculated as 60 multiplied by four, minus 20 marks for incorrect responses.
Since wrong answers reduce the score, candidates should avoid unsupported guessing and manage their time carefully.

sections.heading: VITEEE 2027 MPCEA and BPCEA Exam Patterns

content.text: VITEEE 2027 has two examination streams based on the Mathematics or Biology subject selected by the candidate.

How to Check NIT Trichy CSE Cutoff 2026 on JoSAA?

content.text: The Joint Seat Allocation Authority provides the official opening and closing ranks for engineering admissions. Candidates can check the NIT Trichy Computer Science and Engineering cutoff using the JoSAA 2026 rank portal.

items: Visit the official website at josaa.nic.in.
Open the Opening and Closing Ranks 2026 section.
Select the required counselling round.
Choose NIT as the institute type.
Select National Institute of Technology Tiruchirappalli.
Choose Computer Science and Engineering (4 Years, Bachelor of Technology).
Select the applicable quota, category and gender pool.
Check the opening and closing ranks displayed in the result.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Other State (OS) quota: For General-category OS, Round 1 of 2026 (13 June) closed at rank 1,317, and the final-round 2025 closing rank was 1,449. That makes it one of the toughest NIT CSE seats.

Home State (Tamil Nadu) quota: One report puts the Round 5 closing rank at 4,015 for home state and 1,373 for other state. Round 4 CSE is listed at 1034 to 3812. Home State ranks are much more relaxed than OS ranks.

Check the quota and category: The cutoff differs by quota (HS or OS), category (General, OBC-NCL, SC, ST, EWS) and gender seat type. JoSAA publishes separate opening and closing ranks for each category, so compare yourself against the right row.
Rank and percentile: CSE at OS generally needs a General rank under about 1,500. This is a rough guide, since the final cutoff is only set by the round-wise counselling outcome.

Verify on the official portal: Third-party reporting of final-round figures has been inconsistent, so verify them on the JoSAA OR-CR portal at josaa.nic.in. I couldn’t confirm an official 2026 final-round figure, and some sites mix 2025 and 2026 data.

sections.heading: How to Apply for IIT Madras Ph.D and MS January 2027

The Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IITH) started accepting applications on 21 October 2026. sections.heading: IIT Hyderabad Ph.D Admission 2027 - Overview
IIT Hyderabad Ph.D Admission 2027 - Important Dates
How to Apply for IIT Hyderabad Ph.D Admission 2027?

items: Visit the official Ph.D. admission website at iith.ac.in/phdadmissions.
Read the general eligibility criteria for the January 2027 session.
Choose the department or interdisciplinary research programme relevant to your academic background.
Download and review its departmental brochure.
Click the Apply Here link to open the online admissions portal.
Register or sign in according to the portal instructions.
Select the appropriate Ph.D. admission category and department.
Fill in the required personal and academic information.
Provide the qualification, entrance-test and experience details applicable to your admission category.
Upload the required documents in the prescribed format.
Review the completed application and pay any fee displayed by the portal.
Submit the application before 10 November 2026 at 5 PM IST.
Save the submitted application and acknowledgement for reference.

sections.heading: IIT Hyderabad Ph.D Departments 2027
Important Instructions

items: Check the criteria for the cycle. The next cycle is for the semester beginning Jan 2027. The eligibility criteria and brochure from the July 2026 round are only a reference and might change.

Apply only through the right channel. IIT Hyderabad has a centralized online application portal for Ph.D admission, and candidates must apply through it. The exception is QIP: for QIP admissions you must apply through the AICTE website, not the IITH portal.

Meet the eligibility before applying. In the July 2026 round, Regular Ph.D needed an ME/M.Tech/MS or equivalent with First Class without GATE. An M.Sc. with First Class needed GATE/CSIR/UGC/DST-Inspire or equivalent. Direct Ph.D needed a BE/B.Tech or equivalent from CFIs with a minimum CGPA of 8.0 without GATE. First class means 60% or CGPA 6.0, with 10% relaxation for OBC and 15% for SC/ST. Requirements vary by department.

Expect shortlisting, then a test or interview. For the January round, shortlisted candidates may be invited directly to one or more rounds of online interviews. The written test is typically held in the July round. Departments can also set their own cut-offs.

Keep your funding and documents ready. Students are funded by IITH through Ministry of Education funding. Candidates with INSPIRE or CSIR-UGC NET JRF funding can also apply. Candidates must upload all necessary documents through the online portal at the time of admission. Admissions are provisional until all documents are provided

Eligibility rules: Candidates who didn’t exercise web options in the first phase are not eligible for mop-up. Candidates who joined a seat earlier and are continuing the course can take part.

Deadlines are final: The web options window ran from 5:00 PM on 12 October to 5:00 PM on 14 October 2026. Mop-up is the final counselling round for vacant MBBS seats. Read the prospectus and Government Orders on the KNRUHS website before acting.

sections.heading: How to Attend PJTAU Special Quota Counselling 2026

content.text: PJTAU Special Quota counselling is manual, not online. There is no web-options or online seat-selection process for this round. To participate:

items: Check your category, applicable quota (Non-Farmers/Farmers'/Agriculture Labourers'), and TG EAPCET-2026 rank against the schedule table above to identify your date and time slot.
Visit www.pjtau.edu.in beforehand to check the latest seat availability position.
Report at the University Auditorium, PJTAU, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, at least one hour before your scheduled time.
Carry all original certificates listed above, along with two Xerox copies of relevant certificates if you belong to EWS, BC, SC, or ST categories.
Only one parent/guardian is permitted to accompany the candidate during the counselling process.
Candidates who secure a seat must submit certificates and pay the prescribed fee on the spot to confirm admission.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: Counselling is held manually; it is not conducted online.
Selection under EWS, BC, SC, and ST quotas is subject to clearance of social status by the respective Telangana Government Directorates.
If a candidate attends counselling late, they must submit a letter to the counselling authorities indicating their actual time of arrival.
Candidates who fail to attend on the scheduled date and time cannot claim a seat as per their merit later.
If information or certificates furnished are found to be false, the University will take appropriate legal action.
Candidates/parents should not rely on middlemen or consultants; all seats are filled only through the University's combined counselling.

Candidates may take original certificates back temporarily (by furnishing an undertaking) if they need to attend another counselling, and must return them by the stipulated day, failing which the admission stands cancelled.

sections.heading: How to Apply for KNRUHS B.Sc Nursing 2026-27 Online

items: Visit the official application portal: tsparamed.tsche.in.
Complete Mobile and Email Registration using a valid, active mobile number and email ID; verify both using the OTPs sent to each.
Click Validate - on successful verification, you will be taken to the Registration Form.
Fill in the required details in the Registration Form and click Validate to proceed to the Payment Gateway.

Pay the Registration and Verification fee (Rs. 2,500/- for OC/BC or Rs. 2,000/- for SC/ST, plus bank charges) via the payment gateway. This fee is non-refundable, so verify your eligibility before paying.
On successful payment, note down your registration number for future reference.

Fill in the complete application form, including Intermediate Board details and the number of subjects as applicable to your board (TS/AP Board: 4 subjects; other State Boards: 4 subjects; CBSE/ICSE/NIOS/AISSCE/SSCE/HSCE/APOSS/TOSS: 3 subjects; Inter Vocational with Bridge Course: 2 subjects).
Upload your passport-size photo and signature (each under 100 KB, in JPG/JPEG format).
Click Save and Exit; you may edit your data using the Data Updation link until it is correct.
Click Upload Certificates and upload all required documents listed above.
After uploading all documents, click Save and Print, and take a printout of the filled-in application form for future reference.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Use a Desktop Computer or Laptop with Internet Explorer; do not use mobiles, tabs, or iPads to fill the application.
Do not enter false information - this is liable for criminal action.
Avoid using a slow internet connection while applying.
Keep your mobile phone accessible and do not block SMS, since OTPs and allotment messages are sent via SMS.
Do not refresh or close the page during payment until you receive a "Successful Payment" confirmation message.
No individual intimations will be sent by the University - check the KNRUHS website regularly for updates.
No transfers between colleges are permitted during the course under any circumstances.
The course duration is 4 years; candidates must complete the course within double the duration, i.e., 8 years for the 4YDC course.
Ragging is strictly prohibited and can lead to cancellation of the seat and legal punishment.
Candidates must tick the Anti-Drug undertaking checkbox while applying and submit a signed Anti-Drug Undertaking at the time of admission.

sections.heading: CCMN 2026 Special Round 1- Important Dates

content.text: As per the CCMN 2026 counselling schedule, candidates allotted a seat in special round 1 must complete document upload, express their willingness, and complete withdrawal (if applicable) within the following timeline:

rows: Special round 1 seat allotment result declared
Result out (exact release date/time not stated in the available source; check the official website for the timestamp)
Document upload, willingness (freeze/float/slide) and withdrawal by candidates
Online document verification by allotted institutes
Resolution of queries raised during verification + final willingness/withdrawal

content.text: Candidates should note that these dates apply specifically to the special round 1 cycle of CCMN 2026. Earlier in the counselling process, round 1 allotment took place, followed by round 2 and round 3 allotments, before the counselling moved into the special rounds to fill remaining vacancies.

sections.heading: Who Was Eligible for CCMN 2026 Special Counselling

content.text: CCMN 2026 special round 1 counselling was open to candidates who had already registered for the special CCMN counselling round. Broadly, the general CCMN 2026 eligibility criteria applicable through the counselling process are:

items: Candidates belonging to General, General-EWS, and OBC categories are required to have passed a BSc or equivalent qualifying degree with at least 60% aggregate marks or 6.5 CGPA.
Candidates belonging to reserved categories (SC, ST, PWD) are required to have at least 55% aggregate marks or 6.0 CGPA.
Candidates in the final year of their qualifying degree were also allowed to apply, provided they submit their final mark sheet as required.

For certain programmes at a few participating institutes, special eligibility criteria and restrictions apply — these are listed separately on the CCMN portal under "View Special Eligibility/Restrictions."
A valid IIT JAM 2026 score is mandatory for participation in CCMN 2026 counselling.

sections.heading: Freeze, Float, Slide or Withdraw: What Candidates Can Do

content.text: After checking the special round 1 allotment result, allotted candidates must choose one of the willingness options within the given deadline:

rows: Candidate accepts the currently allotted seat and confirms admission to that institute/programme; no further participation in upcoming rounds.
Candidate accepts the current seat but remains open to a better allotment in subsequent rounds.
Candidate wants to be considered for a different programme within the same or another institute in later rounds while keeping current allotment as backup.
Candidate withdraws entirely from the allotted seat and the counselling process.

content.text: Candidates must also complete online document upload for verification within the same window, since institutes will be verifying submitted documents during this period.

sections.heading: How to Check the CCMN 2026 Special Round 1 Seat Allotment Result

items: Visit the official website: ccmn.admissions.nic.in.
Click on the "CCMN 2026 Special Round 1 Seat Allotment Result" link on the homepage.
Log in using your registered JAM 2026 credentials (registration ID and password).
View your allotted institute, programme, and category status.
Download/save the allotment result for your records.
Proceed to upload the required documents and submit your willingness (freeze/float/slide) or withdrawal option before the deadline.

sections.heading: What Happens After Special Round 1

content.text: The CCMN allotment process for the special rounds is typically followed by a Special Round 2 and then a National Spot Round (NSR), which is the last counselling round in the CCMN cycle. Candidates who take admission through any round are usually required to complete physical reporting at the allotted institute after the process concludes, as per institute-specific instructions.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: Keep your JAM 2026 registration ID and password ready before logging in to check the result.
Complete document upload, verification, and willingness options strictly within the notified deadlines to avoid cancellation of the allotted seat.
Regularly check the official CCMN 2026 website for updates, since institute-wise seat vacancy figures may be revised as candidates upgrade from earlier rounds.
For queries specific to a participating institute's admission process, use the contact details listed on the CCMN portal for that institute.

detail.title: CCMT 2026 Special Round Counselling - Overview
detail.short_info: CCMT 2026 special round seat matrix (vacant seats) has been released by NIT Agartala. Check registration dates, eligibility, application fee, required documents, selection process and how to apply for the CCMT special round counselling for M.Tech/M.Arch/M.Plan admission at NITs, IIITs and GFTIs.

content.text: NIT Agartala, the conducting institute for CCMT (Centralized Counselling for M.Tech/M.Arch/M.Plan Admissions), released the tentative vacant seat matrix for the CCMT 2026 special round on July 13, 2026. Online registration for the special round opens on July 14, 2026. The special round is meant to fill seats that remain vacant at NITs, IIEST Shibpur, IIITs, and other participating GFTIs/CFTIs after the completion of the three regular counselling rounds.

sections.heading: CCMT 2026 Special Round Counselling - Overview

rows: NITs, IIEST Shibpur, select IIITs and CFTIs/GFTIs
Special round vacant seat matrix released; registration begins next

sections.heading: Important Dates

content.text: The table below lists the dates confirmed in official CCMT communications and news coverage. Any date not listed here was not confirmed in the sources reviewed for this article.

rows: Choice filling and locking (regular rounds) closed
Round 3 seat allotment and cutoff released
Special round vacant seat matrix (tentative) released

content.text: Note: The exact closing date for special round registration, the choice-filling window, and the special round seat allotment date were not available in the sources reviewed for this article. Candidates should check the official schedule on ccmt.admissions.nic.in for these dates as soon as they are released.

sections.heading: Who Can Apply for the Special Round

items: Candidates who were not allotted any seat during the regular counselling rounds.
Candidates who did not participate in the regular rounds but hold a valid GATE score.
Candidates whose earlier allotment was cancelled due to non-fulfilment of eligibility conditions.

content.text: All eligible candidates are required to register afresh for the special round and complete choice filling again, even if they had registered in the regular rounds.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria

items: Candidates must hold a valid GATE score from 2024, 2025, or 2026.

Candidates must have passed their qualifying degree with a minimum aggregate of 60% marks or 6.5 CGPA (for General/General-EWS/OBC categories) and 55% marks or 6.0 CGPA (for SC/ST/PwD categories), from a recognized university/institute.
Final-year students awaiting results may participate provisionally, subject to submitting proof of passing within the specified deadline.
NRI candidates with a degree from another country and a valid GATE/JAM score are eligible, provided the qualifying degree is recognized by the Association of Indian Universities (AIU).
Some participating institutes may apply additional, institute-specific eligibility conditions. Candidates should verify this on the respective institute's website.

sections.heading: Application/Registration Fee

content.text: For CCMT counselling registration, the following non-refundable fee structure has been specified officially. Candidates participating in the special round are required to re-register and pay the applicable registration fee again.
In addition, candidates who are allotted a seat and wish to confirm it must pay a seat acceptance fee of ₹30,000, as per the standard CCMT process.

sections.heading: Selection Process

items: Registration: Log in using GATE credentials and complete the special round registration, paying the applicable fee.
Choice Filling and Locking: Select and lock preferred institutes and programs based on the vacant seat matrix.
Seat Allotment: Seats are allotted based on GATE merit, choices filled, and seat availability.
Response (Freeze/Slide/Float): Candidates allotted a seat choose to freeze, slide, or float, depending on whether they want to accept or wait for an upgrade.
Document Verification: Candidates report to the designated reporting centre (physically or online, as specified) for verification.
Reporting to Institute: Candidates report to the allotted institute within the specified deadline to confirm admission, failing which the seat is cancelled.

sections.heading: Required Documents

content.text: Candidates should keep the following documents ready for the document verification and institute reporting stages:

items: Printout of the CCMT registration and choice-filling form
Downloaded provisional seat allotment letter
GATE scorecard (self-attested copy)
Proof of seat acceptance fee payment
Photo ID proof
Class 10 certificate or birth certificate (as proof of age)
Class 12 mark sheet
Qualifying degree mark sheets for all semesters
Migration certificate from the last institute attended
Three passport-size colour photographs
Transfer, conduct, and course completion certificate from the head of the last institute attended
Degree/provisional certificate (if the degree has been awarded)
Category certificate (if applicable, for reserved category candidates)

sections.heading: How to Apply for CCMT 2026 Special Round

items: Visit the official CCMT website: ccmt.admissions.nic.in
Click on the "Candidate Login" or special round registration link once it is activated on July 14, 2026.
Log in using your GATE registration ID, password, and required credentials.
Complete the special round registration form and pay the applicable registration fee online.
Review the vacant seat matrix and fill fresh choices for institutes and programs.
Lock your choices within the deadline specified on the official schedule.
Check the seat allotment result once released, and proceed with freeze/slide/float, document verification, and reporting as instructed.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: Registration and choice filling for the special round must be completed afresh, even by candidates who registered in earlier rounds.
The vacant seat matrix released on July 13, 2026, is described as tentative; candidates should recheck the matrix for updates before finalizing choices.
Candidates who secured a seat in an earlier round but selected "surrender and participate in next round" may also be eligible for the special round, based on official eligibility conditions.
The registration fee is non-refundable.
Candidates should keep their GATE registration ID, password, and security PIN ready for login.
Always cross-check dates, fees, and eligibility on the official CCMT website, as counselling schedules are subject to revision.

detail.title: What is CCMN Counselling 2026?
detail.short_info: Complete guide to CCMN Counselling 2026 registration dates, seat allotment results, counselling fees, documents required, participating NITs, and step-by-step procedure for M.Sc. admissions via IIT JAM scores.

content.text: CCMN (Centralized Counselling for M.Sc./M.Sc. Tech) 2026 is the official centralised admission process through which IIT JAM-qualified candidates can secure seats in M.Sc. and M.Sc. Tech programmes offered by 20 NITs and other Centrally Funded Technical Institutes (CFTIs) across India. Conducted by NIT Warangal, the CCMN 2026 process covers online registration, choice filling, seat allotment, document verification, and physical reporting all carried out in multiple rounds. The CCMN 2026 first seat allotment result was released on June 12, 2026, and document verification must be completed by June 17, 2026. The second seat allotment is scheduled for June 22, 2026.

sections.heading: What is CCMN Counselling 2026?

content.text: CCMN counselling is the centralised seat-allocation mechanism for postgraduate science programmes at NITs and CFTIs in India. This section gives you the complete picture of what CCMN is and how it works.

CCMN stands for Centralized Counselling for M.Sc./M.Sc. Tech. Administered by NIT Warangal on behalf of all participating institutes, it uses candidates' IIT JAM 2026 scores to allocate seats across M.Sc. programmes in subjects such as Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Data Science, Biotechnology, and more. The process is conducted entirely online through the official NIC portal. The CCMN counselling process 2026 consists of registration, choice filling, seat allotment, and payment confirmation, with the goal of providing admissions for M.Sc. programmes at 20 NITs and CFTIs.

sections.heading: CCMN 2026 Counselling Dates Complete Schedule

content.text: Staying on top of all important dates is critical for securing a seat through CCMN 2026. Below is the complete schedule across all three phases.

sections.heading: Phase I: Regular Rounds Schedule

rows: Online Registration, Fee Payment & Choice Filling Opens

Round 3: SAF Payment, Document Upload & Withdrawal

rows: Last Date for Registration & Fee Payment

sections.heading: CCMN 2026 Eligibility Criteria

content.text: Understanding who can participate in CCMN 2026 counselling is the first step before beginning the registration process.

To be eligible for CCMN counselling 2026, students need to have appeared for the JAM exam with a valid score. From the list of courses offered by different universities, they can select programmes based on admission requirements. Candidates must also check the individual eligibility conditions of each programme they wish to apply for before submitting the CCMN 2026 application, since subject-specific requirements may vary across NITs and CFTIs.

sections.heading: CCMN Counselling Fees 2026

content.text: CCMN 2026 involves several fee components that candidates must pay at different stages of the process. Here is a complete breakdown.
The CCMN 2026 counselling fees are structured as follows:
Note: The SAF, PAF, and participation fees are adjusted against the total course admission fee, making them partly recoverable.

sections.heading: CCMN Counselling Procedure 2026 Step-by-Step Guide

content.text: The CCMN 2026 counselling procedure follows a clearly defined sequence of steps. Here is exactly what candidates need to do at each stage.

sections.heading: Step 1: CCMN Registration 2026

content.text: Candidates must complete the CCMN application form with personal details including gender, JAM score, mobile number, email address, paper code, and registration number. The registration fee can be paid through the ICICI bank Eazypay system. Providing false information on the application form will lead to disqualification from consideration for admission.

sections.heading: Step 2: CCMN Choice Filling 2026

content.text: Before the submission deadline, candidates must complete the CCMN 2026 application form for counselling by selecting their preferred programme and institution. Candidates are presented with a list of options during the process and must rank them in order of priority. Choices can be modified before final submission, but if candidates forget to lock their choices before the deadline, they will be locked automatically.

sections.heading: Step 3: CCMN Seat Allotment 2026

content.text: The CCMN 2026 seat allocation list is created using the candidates' choices and JAM scores. Candidates can view the seat allotment result using their IIT JAM registration ID and password. To accept the allotted seat, candidates should select the "Freeze" option. Upon accepting the seat allotment, candidates must pay the admission fee and report to the counselling location. A provisional admission notification will be issued to candidates who have frozen their seats and paid the CCMN counselling participation fee. Candidates can also withdraw their seats following the first and second allotment rounds.

sections.heading: Step 4: Document Verification

content.text: After the seat allotment, candidates must upload documents online and complete verification through the allotted institute. Physical reporting at the finally allotted institute takes place as per the schedule of each round.

sections.heading: CCMN National Spot Round 2026

content.text: The National Spot Round (NSR) is an additional opportunity for candidates who missed out on seats in the regular rounds. Here is what you need to know.

CCMN National Spot Round 2026 counselling will take place tentatively from August 1. Candidates must fill out and submit the CCMN choice filling form and complete registration before the submission deadline. The NSR is held only after the completion of all three regular rounds of CCMN seat allotment 2026.

sections.heading: Who is Eligible for the NSR?

content.text: Eligibility for the National Spot Round is limited to the following categories of candidates: those who have not yet completed the CCMN application form 2026; those who registered for CCMN 2026 but were not allocated a seat in any round; candidates who were given a seat in an earlier round but did not pay the counselling fee; and candidates who withdrew their seats in the first, second, or third rounds of allotment.

sections.heading: Documents Required for CCMN Counselling 2026

content.text: Having the correct documents ready in advance prevents last-minute delays during the verification stage. Below is the complete list of documents required.
The following documents are required for CCMN 2026 counselling:

items: Class 10th marksheet and certificate
Class 12th marksheet and certificate
IIT JAM 2026 scorecard
Printout of the registration form with locked choices

Character certificate
Provisional admission letter
Transfer certificate
Qualifying degree certificate
Passport-size photographs

sections.heading: What to Do After CCMT Round 1 Seat Allotment 2026?

content.text: Once the result is out, candidates must take action promptly. Here is everything you need to do after checking your allotment.

Once the seat is allocated, candidates must complete their online reporting process within the deadline. They will have to pay their seat acceptance fee and choose one of the available willingness options.
After reviewing the allotment, candidates must select one of the following three options:

sections.heading: Option 1 : Freeze

content.text: If you are fully satisfied with the allotted seat, choose Freeze. This confirms your admission to the allotted institute and branch. Once candidates freeze the option, they do not participate in subsequent rounds of counselling for seat upgradation.

sections.heading: Option 2 - Float

content.text: Choose Float if you want to retain your current allotment but also wish to be considered for a higher-preference choice in upcoming rounds. If a better seat is available in Round 2 or 3, it will be automatically upgraded; otherwise, the current seat is retained.

sections.heading: Option 3 - Slide

content.text: Choose Slide if you want to be upgraded to a better branch within the same institute in subsequent rounds. Your current seat is retained if no upgrade is available.

sections.heading: Option 4 - Surrender

content.text: Candidates can also surrender the currently allotted seat and participate only in the next round for better-preferred choices. However, a warning applies: if no seat is allotted in the next round, the surrendered seat is permanently lost.

sections.heading: CCMT 2026 Round 1 Cutoff - What to Expect

content.text: The Round 1 cutoff represents the minimum GATE score needed to secure admission to a specific institute and branch combination.

Along with the seat allotment, official opening and closing CCMT Round 1 cutoff scores for all participating institutes will be uploaded at ccmt.admissions.nic.in. The CCMT 2026 Round 1 cutoff will depend on factors such as GATE score difficulty, total CCMT 2026 seat matrix, and the preferences locked by candidates.

sections.heading: JEECUP Pharmacy Round 4 Freeze and Float Options

content.text: After receiving a provisional seat allotment, candidates must select their willingness option through the JEECUP candidate dashboard.

rows: Accept the currently allotted seat without seeking an upgrade.
Retain the current allotment while requesting consideration for a higher-preference seat in a subsequent round, subject to counselling rules.

Candidates should select their willingness carefully because it affects participation in further allotment rounds.

sections.heading: JEECUP Pharmacy Round 4 Security Fee Payment Last Date

content.text: Allotted candidates must pay the applicable seat acceptance or security fee through the official counselling system.
The scheduled payment period is 22-24 October 2026, with the Round 4 deadline at 5 PM on 24 October.
The official JEECUP allotment instructions state that failure to pay the prescribed seat acceptance fee can lead to cancellation of the allotted seat.

The exact payable amount should be checked in the candidate's counselling dashboard and current official fee instructions. Candidates should not assume that the registration fee, counselling fee and security fee are identical.

Document verification confirms academic eligibility, category claims and other admission details before the admission process is completed.

Select Freeze or Float according to the counselling rules.
Pay the prescribed security or seat acceptance fee.
Complete document verification if required under the selected option.
Check the available admission or reporting instructions.

Retain the admission and payment acknowledgements.

Registration is mandatory: Only registered candidates are eligible to receive admit cards and appear in the board exams. Students should confirm with their school that registration was completed.

This is the fifth and final round of JoSAA counselling for 2026, through which seats are allotted to candidates for admission into IITs, NITs, IIITs, and Government Funded Technical Institutes (GFTIs) based on JEE Main and JEE Advanced 2026 ranks. rows: Round 5 Reporting and Fee Payment Deadline

content.text: These dates are based on the official JoSAA 2026 counselling schedule. Candidates should verify the latest updates directly on josaa.nic.in, as authorities occasionally revise deadlines.

sections.heading: JoSAA Round 5: How to Check the Seat Allotment Result

content.text: Candidates can follow these steps to check and download their JoSAA Round 5 seat allotment result 2026:

items: Visit the official website: josaa.nic.in.
Click on the "Seat Allotment Result" link active for Round 5.
Log in using your JEE Main 2026 application number and password (JEE Advanced candidates use the same JoSAA login).
Your Round 5 allotment status will be displayed, showing allotted institute, branch, category, and rank details.
If a seat has been allotted, download the Provisional Seat Allotment Letter / Initial Seat Allotment Intimation Slip.
Save a digital copy and print multiple physical copies for reporting and document verification.

content.text: Important: JoSAA does not send individual result notifications to candidates. It is each candidate's own responsibility to log in and check their allotment status for every round, including Round 5.

sections.heading: What Happens After the JoSAA Round 5 Result?

content.text: Once the Round 5 result is out, allotted candidates must choose one of the following options within the deadline:

rows: Accept the current seat but remain open to an upgrade in institute/branch. Since Round 5 is the final round, floating candidates will not get further upgrades through JoSAA and must proceed with reporting.
Accept the seat and lock it in permanently, with no further upgrade sought.
Confirm the current allotment while remaining open to a better course within the same institute.
Completely withdraw from JoSAA counselling. A processing fee (as specified in the official brochure) is deducted from the seat acceptance amount.

content.text: Because Round 5 is the last round of JoSAA counselling for 2026, candidates who float will not be moved to another seat afterward through JoSAA - they must still complete reporting for their current allotment to retain it.

sections.heading: Eligibility for JoSAA Seat Allotment

items: For IIT admission: A valid JEE Advanced 2026 rank is mandatory. Candidates must also be among the top 2.5 lakh JEE Main qualifiers to have been eligible for JEE Advanced.

For NIT/IIIT/GFTI admission: A valid JEE Main 2026 rank is required, along with either 75% marks in Class 12 (65% for SC/ST/PwD candidates) or a position in the top 20 percentile of the respective board.

content.text: Candidates who do not meet the minimum Class 12 qualifying criteria are not eligible for seat allotment at NITs, IIITs, and GFTIs, even if they hold a valid JEE Main rank.

sections.heading: Documents Required for JoSAA Round 5 Reporting

items: JEE Main 2026 admit card/rank card
JEE Advanced 2026 rank card (for IIT-allotted candidates)
Class 10 certificate (for date of birth proof)
Class 12 marksheet and pass certificate
Category certificate - SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS (if applicable)
PwD certificate (if applicable)
Passport-size photographs (scanned, as per prescribed format)
Scanned signature (as per prescribed format)

content.text: All documents must match JoSAA's prescribed file format and size specifications, which are listed in the official information brochure on josaa.nic.in.

sections.heading: Seat Vacancy and Cutoff Details for Round 5

content.text: Institute-wise and branch-wise vacancy numbers, along with the opening and closing ranks for Round 5, are published separately by JoSAA on its official Opening/Closing Rank (OR-CR) portal shortly after each round's result. These figures were not available in the sources reviewed for this article at the time of writing. Candidates should check the OR-CR section on josaa.nic.in directly for the confirmed Round 5 opening and closing ranks for their category and preferred institute.

Note: Opening/Closing Ranks for "Open" category seats represent the Common Rank List (CRL), while those for EWS, OBC-NCL, SC, and ST represent category-specific ranks. A rank suffixed with 'P' indicates it is from the Preparatory Rank List.

sections.heading: Fee Details

content.text: The exact seat acceptance fee amount for JoSAA Round 5, 2026 was not confirmed in the sources available for this article. Only the processing fee for a complete withdrawal/surrender (₹3,000, deducted from the seat acceptance amount) is specified in available reports. Candidates should refer to the official JoSAA 2026 information brochure or the fee payment section on josaa.nic.in for the exact applicable amount.

sections.heading: What Happens if You Miss the Round 5 Deadline?

content.text: If a candidate fails to complete seat acceptance, reporting, and fee payment within the Round 5 deadline (July 21, 2026), their candidature is permanently cancelled for JoSAA counselling, and they will not be considered in any further JoSAA round, since Round 5 is the last round. Such candidates may still be eligible to participate in CSAB special counselling rounds, which are conducted separately to fill vacant seats at NITs, IIITs, and GFTIs after JoSAA concludes.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for Candidates

items: Round 5 is the final round of JoSAA Counselling 2026 - there is no subsequent JoSAA round after this.

Always use the Float option (not Surrender) if you wish to remain eligible for admission while hoping for a better outcome elsewhere, since Freeze-to-Float switching is not allowed but Float-to-Freeze is.
Complete document upload and respond to any verification queries within the specified deadline, or risk elimination from counselling.
Keep both digital and printed copies of the Provisional Seat Allotment Letter ready, as it is mandatory for physical reporting at the allotted institute.
In case of allotment change between the IIT system and the NIT+ system, candidates must report to the newly changed institute; failing to do so cancels the allotted seat.

Any queries related to IIT/IISc admissions should be directed to the JoSAA IIT Roorkee team; queries related to the NIT+ system should go to the CSAB team, as per contact details published on josaa.nic.in. Responses must be submitted only through the JoSAA portal, not by email.

items.name: What Is the JoSAA Round 3 Cutoff 2026?

detail.title: What Is the JoSAA Round 3 Cutoff 2026?
detail.short_info: JoSAA Round 3 cutoff 2026 is out on josaa.nic.in. Check IIT, NIT, IIIT & GFTI opening-closing ranks, reporting deadline, SAF fee & Freeze/Float/Slide options.

content.text: The Joint Seat Allocation Authority (JoSAA) released the Round 3 seat allotment result and cutoff for the 2026 academic session on July 6, 2026, at 5:00 PM IST on the official portal, josaa.nic.in. The Round 3 cutoff is expressed as opening and closing ranks the range of JEE Main or JEE Advanced ranks within which a seat was offered in a specific institute, branch, category, and quota. If your rank falls within this range, your seat allotment for that combination is confirmed for this round.

This article explains what the JoSAA Round 3 cutoff means, how to check it institute-wise on the official website, how ranks are trending compared to earlier rounds, and exactly what candidates need to do next from paying the seat acceptance fee to choosing Freeze, Float, or Slide.

sections.heading: What Is the JoSAA Round 3 Cutoff 2026?

content.text: The JoSAA cutoff is not a fixed number it's a rank band published separately for every institute, academic program, quota, category, and gender combination after each counselling round. Round 3 cutoffs specifically reflect the seats that became available after Round 1 and Round 2 candidates froze, floated, withdrew, or failed to complete reporting.

items: Opening rank: the best (lowest numerical) rank at which a seat was offered in that particular institute-branch combination.
Closing rank: the last (highest numerical) rank at which the final seat was allotted in that round.
Ranks for IITs are based on the JEE Advanced 2026 All India Rank, while NITs, IIITs, and GFTIs use the JEE Main 2026 Common Rank List (CRL) or category rank.

Opening rank is the first rank that secured admission in a particular college and branch, while closing rank is the last rank that got admission for instance, if a branch's closing rank is 5,000, every candidate ranked up to 5,000 was eligible for that seat.

sections.heading: JoSAA Round 3 2026 - Key Dates at a Glance

content.text: Knowing the exact counselling timeline is critical, since JoSAA does not grant extensions for missed deadlines. The table below summarizes the confirmed schedule around Round 3.

rows: Online reporting (fee payment, document upload, willingness selection)

content.text: The last date to pay the seat acceptance fee and upload documents is July 8, 2026, at 5:00 PM IST, and verification queries must be answered by July 9, 2026. Round 4 results are expected on July 10, 2026, with a reporting deadline of July 12, while Round 5, the final round, is expected on July 16, 2026, with reporting closing on July 18. Candidates should treat Round 4 and 5 dates as provisional until JoSAA confirms them after Round 3 reporting closes.

sections.heading: How Many Institutes and Seats Are Part of JoSAA 2026?

content.text: Understanding the scale of the counselling process helps candidates gauge how competitive Round 3 cutoffs are likely to be across different institute categories.

JoSAA 2026 manages joint seat allocation for admission to 138 institutes for the academic year 2026-27, comprising 23 IITs, IISc Bengaluru, 31 NITs, IIEST Shibpur, 26 IIITs, and 56 Other Government-Funded Technical Institutes (Other-GFTIs). On the seat-availability side, a total of 64,219 engineering seats are available for BTech admissions this year, plus 3,104 supernumerary seats reserved specifically for female candidates, with NITs alone contributing the largest share at 25,162 seats.

sections.heading: How to Check JoSAA Round 3 Cutoff 2026 Online

content.text: The official JoSAA opening and closing rank (OR-CR) portal lets candidates filter cutoff data by institute, program, category, and round. Here's the step-by-step process to pull up your specific cutoff:

items: Visit the official portal at josaa.nic.in.
Click on the eServices (or Services) tab on the homepage menu.
Select the OR-CR link, and choose "OR-CR 2026" for the current cycle.

In the filter form, select: Round No. choose Round 3 Type of Institute IIT, NIT, IIIT, or GFTI Name of the Institute your target college Academic Program the specific branch (e.g., Computer Science, Mechanical) Seat Type/Category OPEN, OBC-NCL, SC, ST, or EWS as applicable
Round No. choose Round 3
Type of Institute IIT, NIT, IIIT, or GFTI
Name of the Institute your target college
Academic Program the specific branch (e.g., Computer Science, Mechanical)
Seat Type/Category OPEN, OBC-NCL, SC, ST, or EWS as applicable
Click Submit to view the opening rank and closing rank table for that exact combination.

content.text: The JoSAA 2026 cutoff PDFs list the institute name, academic program, quota, seat type, gender, opening rank, and closing rank, and this data is released for all 138 participating institutes. Shiksha

links.text: Shiksha

sections.heading: Round 3 Cutoff Trends: IIT vs NIT vs IIIT vs GFTI

content.text: Cutoff movement between rounds varies significantly depending on the institute type, and understanding this pattern helps candidates decide whether to Float for an upgrade or Freeze their current seat.

items: IITs: Closing ranks for top branches at premier IITs tend to barely shift across rounds. At IIT Bombay, Delhi, and Madras, Computer Science closing ranks show almost no movement across all five rounds because candidates in this rank range overwhelmingly prefer these seats, and very few vacate them. Cracku

NITs: These typically see the sharpest relaxation in Round 3. NIT seats consistently relax by 8 to 15% by Round 3, as candidates who were allotted IIT seats confirm and exit, freeing up NIT options for those just outside the Round 1 cutoff. Note that NIT cutoffs are released separately for Home State and Other State quota, so check the correct column for your domicile. CrackuMotion Blog

IIITs and GFTIs: IIITs and GFTIs also base their cutoffs on JEE Main ranks, and while GFTIs are often overlooked, several of them offer strong placement records in core engineering branches. Motion Blog

content.text: Because these estimated relaxation patterns are historical trends and not confirmed figures, always cross-check the actual Round 3 numbers published on josaa.admissions.nic.in before making a Freeze or Float decision.

sections.heading: What to Do After the Round 3 Allotment: Freeze, Float, or Slide

content.text: Once your Round 3 result is out, you must choose one of three willingness options and complete online reporting skipping this step is treated as a rejection of your seat.

items: Freeze: Choose this if your allotted seat is your genuine first choice. Freezing is final you exit the counselling process and cannot participate in Rounds 4 or 5.
Float: Keeps you eligible for a possible upgrade to a better institute or branch in Round 4 and Round 5, while safely retaining your current seat if no upgrade comes through.
Slide: Keeps you within the same institute but eligible for a preferred branch upgrade.

content.text: Float is generally the safer decision unless your current allotment is your absolute first preference, since it carries zero downgrade risk if no upgrade happens in later rounds, you simply keep your existing seat.

sections.heading: Seat Acceptance Fee (SAF) and Reporting Requirements

items: The Seat Acceptance Fee is Rs. 30,000 for General, OBC-NCL, and EWS categories, and Rs. 15,000 for SC, ST, and PwD categories.
Of this, Rs. 5,000 is a non-refundable processing charge, while the remainder is adjusted against the institute's admission fee.
If you already paid the SAF in an earlier round, it carries forward automatically, and only first-time allottees in Round 3 need to make a fresh payment.

Required documents typically include your Class 10 and 12 certificates, JEE Main/Advanced admit card and scorecard, category/PwD certificates (if applicable), a medical certificate, and passport-size photographs.

A common rejection reason: OBC-NCL and EWS certificates issued even one day before April 1, 2026, are treated as invalid and can lead to immediate seat cancellation get a fresh certificate if yours predates this.

sections.heading: What Happens Next: JoSAA Round 4 and Round 5

content.text: If you don't secure a seat in Round 3, there's no need to worry about re-registering. Candidates without an allotment in Round 3 automatically remain in the process for Rounds 4 and 5 at no additional cost. If your willingness status is set to Float or Slide, you also remain fully eligible for a further upgrade in the subsequent rounds. After Round 5 concludes, any seats that remain vacant across NITs, IIITs, and GFTIs move to the CSAB Special Round for a final round of counselling.

Number of seats available for each course

content.text: The HNBUMU Admit Card 2026 for the Uttarakhand BSc Nursing Entrance Exam has been officially released by Hemwati Nandan Bahuguna Uttarakhand Medical Education University. Candidates who completed the application process can now download their Uttarakhand BSc Nursing Admit Card 2026 directly from the official portal at hnbumu.ac.in. content.text: Violating any of these rules can lead to disqualification:

Follow all invigilator instructions during the exam

items: Provisional Answer Key - Candidates can raise objections if any answer seems incorrect
Final Answer Key - Released after reviewing objections
HNBUMU BSc Nursing Result 2026 - Merit list published on hnbumu.ac.in
Counselling Schedule - Eligible candidates invited for document verification and seat selection
Seat Allotment List - Final college and seat allotted based on rank and preference
Bookmark the official HNBUMU website to stay updated on each of these stages after the exam.

sections.heading: Last-Minute Preparation Tips for Uttarakhand BSc Nursing Entrance 2026

content.text: With only days left before the 13 June exam, here's what matters most:

items: Revise Biology first it carries the highest weightage in nursing entrance exams
Practice solving previous year HNBUMU BSc Nursing papers under timed conditions
Focus on Human Anatomy, Physiology, and Microbiology topics
For Chemistry, revise Organic basics and Biomolecules
Avoid picking up new heavy topics in the final 48 hours consolidate what you already know
Sleep well the night before and eat a light meal on exam morning

sections.heading: About the HNBUMU BSc Nursing Entrance Exam 2026

content.text: HNBUMU (Hemwati Nandan Bahuguna Uttarakhand Medical Education University) is the apex medical education authority in Uttarakhand, responsible for conducting entrance exams for nursing and allied health courses across government and private colleges in the state.

The Uttarakhand BSc Nursing Entrance Exam 2026 determines admission to 4-year BSc Nursing degree programs offered at colleges affiliated to HNBUMU. The exam is OMR-based and tests candidates on subjects including Biology, Physics, Chemistry, and General Knowledge/Nursing Aptitude.
Candidates who qualify the entrance exam will proceed to the HNBUMU BSc Nursing counselling process, where seats are allotted based on merit rank and college preferences.

content.text: Students should regularly check the official website for any updates or changes to this schedule and remember that the response sheet is usually released before the provisional answer key.

sections.heading: How to Use JEE Advanced Response Sheet 2026 to Estimate Score

content.text: The primary purpose of the JEE Advanced response sheet is to let candidates verify their marked responses and estimate their probable score before the results are out. Once the provisional answer key is released, candidates can compare each response with the official correct answer to calculate their marks.
Matching Responses with Provisional Answer Key
After downloading the response sheet, candidates should wait for the provisional answer key, which is scheduled to be published on May 25, 2026. When both documents are available, you can:

items: Place the response sheet and provisional answer key side by side.
For each question, check whether your recorded response matches the correct option in the answer key.
Note questions left unattempted and those where you might have chosen an incorrect option.

content.text: This process helps you understand your performance in each section and identify topics where you did well or need improvement.
Calculating Probable Marks
JEE Advanced uses its own marking scheme, including full, partial and negative marks depending on the question type. Using the response sheet and answer key:

items: Add marks for each correct response as per the marking scheme for that particular question.
Subtract marks for questions with negative marking if your response does not match the correct answer.
Sum the scores for all questions across Paper 1 and Paper 2 to get an approximate total.

content.text: This estimated score is only indicative and the final score will be based on the official evaluation and final answer key.

sections.heading: JEE Advanced 2026 Exam - Basic Details (For Reference)

content.text: JEE Advanced is conducted for admission to undergraduate programmes in engineering, sciences and architecture at the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs). For 2026, IIT Roorkee is the organising institute and the exam consists of two compulsory papers conducted on the same day.

Each paper typically includes questions from Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, with a mix of single-correct, multiple-correct and numerical answer types. Candidates must appear in both Paper 1 and Paper 2 to be considered for ranking, and the total score is calculated based on performance in both papers combined.

sections.heading: Important Instructions for JEE Advanced 2026 Candidates

content.text: Candidates should follow certain important instructions while checking their JEE Advanced 2026 response sheet and using it for evaluation.

items: Ensure you download response sheets for both Paper 1 and Paper 2 and verify that your name and roll number are correctly mentioned.
Always download the response sheet from the official website only and avoid sharing your login details with others.
Save the PDF on a secure device and consider taking a printout for easy comparison with the provisional answer key.

sections.heading: GATE COAP 2026 Eligibility Criteria

content.text: This section answers “who should register for COAP 2026”.
GATE Score Requirements

items: You must have a valid GATE score in at least one of the following years: 2024, 2025, or 2026.
If you have multiple valid GATE scores (for example GATE 2025 and GATE 2026), you should use the scorecard with the higher score or better rank while registering.

content.text: Other Basic Conditions

items: COAP is meant for Indian citizens; foreign nationals usually apply directly to IITs without using COAP.
COAP registration is compulsory for candidates seeking M.Tech/M.Plan/M.Des admission to participating IITs through GATE, because the offers are displayed only through this portal.
COAP does not replace the individual IIT application: you still need to fill separate programme‑wise forms on each IIT’s admission portal.

sections.heading: Documents and Details Required for GATE COAP 2026 Registration

content.text: Help users prepare everything in advance so registration is smooth.
Details You Must Have

items: GATE Registration/Enrollment ID.
GATE paper code, year of exam, and GATE score as per your scorecard.
Full name, date of birth, category, and other personal details exactly as in the GATE form.
Valid email ID and active mobile number for OTPs and alerts.

content.text: Useful Documents to Keep Ready

items: PDF / screenshot of the latest GATE scorecard.
A list of IITs and programmes you are planning to apply to (for later use on IIT portals, not at COAP).

sections.heading: How to Register for GATE COAP 2026 (Step‑by‑Step)

content.text: This is the main transactional section for “GATE COAP 2026 registration kaise kare”.
Direct COAP 2026 Registration Link

items: COAP 2026 Portal: Click Here

content.text: Place this link near the top and again here in your article for better CTR.
Step‑by‑Step GATE COAP 2026 Registration Process

items: Visit the COAP 2026 portal Open your browser and go to the official COAP 2026 website (coap2026.iitr.ac.in/coap2026/).
Click on “Register” / “New User Registration” On the home page, click the registration button for new candidates.
Enter GATE details Fill in your GATE Registration/Enrollment ID, GATE paper code, year of exam, and GATE score as printed on the scorecard.
Fill personal information Enter your name, date of birth, category, email ID, and mobile number exactly as per your GATE records to avoid mismatch issues.
Create login credentials Set a strong password, confirm it, and enter the captcha/security code shown on screen.
Submit and verify Submit the registration form. Note down the COAP 2026 Registration ID displayed on screen and sent to your email/mobile.
Login to COAP account Use your COAP Registration ID and password to log in, verify your details, and keep the credentials safely for use during every round.

content.text: You can also add a note: “There is usually no separate fee for COAP registration; any fee you pay is for the individual IIT application forms, not for COAP itself.”

sections.heading: What to Do After GATE COAP 2026 Registration

content.text: Many students are confused after registering, so this section adds real value.
Two Parallel Steps for IIT M.Tech Admission

items: Step 1: Register on COAP (this portal). This is required only once and creates your central offer‑view account.

Step 2: Apply to individual IITs separately. Visit each participating IIT’s admission website (IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, IIT Madras, IIT Roorkee, etc.), fill their M.Tech/M.Plan/M.Des application forms, pay the institute‑specific fee, and mention your GATE details and COAP registration where asked.

content.text: COAP will show offers only from those institutes and programmes where you have already applied directly and been considered based on GATE.
Using COAP 2026 in Every Round

items: During each active round window, log in to the COAP portal with your Registration ID and password.
Check all the offers displayed from different IITs and programmes (if any).

For each round, choose one of the decision options provided on the portal, commonly: Accept & Freeze - Accept one offer and exit further COAP rounds for that programme. Retain & Wait - Keep your current best offer but remain eligible for upgrade in later rounds. Reject & Wait - Reject the current offer(s) and wait for potential new/ better offers in the next rounds.

detail.short_info: IIM Calcutta MBA Admission 2027-29 policy released. Check CAT 2026 minimum cut-offs, eligibility, PI and WAT weightage, and selection criteria.

content.text: The Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Calcutta has released its admission policy for the two-year full-time MBA programme for the 2027-29 batch. Admission will be based on CAT 2026, scheduled for 29 November 2026, followed by shortlisting, a Personal Interview (PI) and a Writing Ability Test (WAT). The minimum overall CAT percentile for Open category candidates is 85, along with the prescribed sectional cut-offs.

sections.heading: IIM Calcutta MBA Admission 2027-29 - Overview
IIM Calcutta MBA Admission 2027-29 Important Dates
IIM Calcutta CAT 2026 Cut Off for MBA Admission 2027-29
How to Apply for IIM Calcutta MBA Admission 2027-29?

content.text: Domestic candidates seeking admission to the two-year full-time MBA programme are considered through CAT 2026. IIM Calcutta does not conduct a separate entrance examination for this admission route.

items: Register for CAT 2026 through the official CAT admission process within the prescribed registration period.
Indicate IIM Calcutta and its MBA programme in the applicable CAT registration preferences.
Appear for CAT 2026 on 29 November 2026.
Check the CAT result and verify the minimum sectional and overall percentile requirements.
Check the IIM Calcutta website for the PI-WAT shortlist.
Complete the additional application and document requirements communicated to shortlisted candidates.
Attend the Personal Interview and Writing Ability Test on the allotted schedule.
Check the final admission decision and follow the institute's admission instructions if selected.

sections.heading: Important Instructions

items: CAT 2026 is your entry exam. The route is CAT 2026 on 29 November 2026, and there is no separate application before then. You are also asked to register for CAT with the IIM Calcutta details in your profile, since the institute uses CAT data.

Selection has three stages. The 2027 process has three stages. One report says CAT carries 56 points in shortlisting and the personal interview (PI) carries 48% of the final selection. Another says PI gets 48% and the CAT score 30% in the final composite. Don’t rely on either figure until you’ve read the official policy.

Minimum CAT percentile and graduation marks apply. Stage I has a minimum CAT percentile for the 2027-29 batch (CAT 2026 score), and graduation marks thresholds also apply. Meeting the minimum doesn’t guarantee a shortlist.
Final-year students can apply, with a deadline. The final-year degree certificate submission deadline is 30 June 2027. If you’re still in your final year, plan your result timing around it.

Overseas applicants have a separate GMAT route. It needs a GMAT total of at least 735 with at least 89 in Verbal, Quantitative and Data Insights; the application fee is USD 150 and the last date is 1 February 2027. Shortlists are expected in the first week of January 2027, so watch your registered email.

sections.heading: CSAB 2026 Mock Seat Allotment - Allotment Process

items: Candidates register and fill/reorder institute-branch preferences on the CSAB portal.
The mock seat allotment is generated based on current preferences, JEE Main 2026 rank, category, and available seats - this shows candidates their probable allotment.
Candidates can review the mock result and revise their preference order during the editing window.
Once satisfied, candidates must lock their final choices by August 5, 2026 (2 PM); choice locking requires OTP verification sent to the registered mobile number and email ID.
After locking, no further edits are permitted for Round 1.

sections.heading: How to Check CSAB 2026 Mock Seat Allotment Result
