content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Recruitment 2026 Important Dates
content_sections.text: Online registration for Nagaland Police Constable GD Recruitment 2026 will begin on 31 October 2026. Candidates must complete the application and pay the examination fee by the closing date of 30 November 2026. Admit cards will be generated after successful completion of the online application and may be downloaded immediately thereafter. Written examination and interview schedules will be communicated through the official Nagaland Police website and local newspapers.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: Nagaland Police has advertised 1,137 Constable GD vacancies. Of these, 1,053 vacancies are allocated through the current recruitment under the approved tribal ratio, while 84 are backlog vacancies from the previous recruitment.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable District-wise Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: The 1,053 regular recruitment vacancies are distributed among participating districts according to the approved tribal ratio based on the 2011 Census. The district allocation also includes separate male and female vacancies. The original notification provides detailed tribe-wise allocations within these districts in Annexure I. Applicants must check the specific tribe and district allocation before selecting their application district.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Backlog Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: The notification also provides 84 backlog Constable GD vacancies reserved for specific tribes and districts whose vacancies remained unfilled in the preceding recruitment. All 84 backlog vacancies are allocated to male candidates. Special Condition: The single Phom backlog vacancy under Mokokchung is restricted to eligible members of the Phom tribe belonging to Anaki (Old) and Anaki 'C' villages. Candidates applying for backlog posts must satisfy the exact district, residence and tribe conditions provided in Annexure III.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Eligibility Criteria 2026
content_sections.text: The educational qualification for Nagaland Police Constable GD Recruitment 2026 depends on the applicant's tribe classification. Candidates must also possess valid documents establishing their Indigenous Inhabitant and tribal eligibility. The educational qualification must be from a recognized board or educational authority. Where a pass certificate or provisional pass certificate has not been issued, the notification requires an appropriate certificate or letter from the concerned educational institution or authority. The recruitment is open to eligible male and female candidates from Indigenous Inhabitant Tribes of Nagaland who meet the prescribed age, education, district and physical fitness requirements. Applicants must possess an Indigenous Inhabitant Certificate and relevant tribal certificates issued by the competent authority. Eligible natives or residents of Dimapur, Chumoukedima and Niuland can apply under the combined allocation for these three districts, provided they possess the prescribed supporting certificates. The notification also provides specific arrangements for members of the Chang, Sumi and Phom tribes from identified villages in Mokokchung, Wokha and Shamator districts. Candidates affected by these provisions should refer to the detailed conditions in the official notification.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Age Limit 2026
content_sections.text: Serving Government employees may receive upper-age relaxation equivalent to their qualifying service, subject to a maximum of five years and the applicable Government policy. The notification also provides age-relaxation conditions for certain incumbent Nagaland Police Constables and petitioners covered by the specified Gauhati High Court judgments and orders.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Salary 2026
content_sections.text: The advertised Constable GD posts carry Pay Level 3, with Grade Pay Rs. 1,800 under the specified pay-band structure of Rs. 5,200–20,200.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Application Fee 2026
content_sections.text: The examination fee for Nagaland Police Constable Recruitment 2026 is Rs. 300 . Applicants must pay the fee online as part of the application process.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: Selection for the Constable GD posts involves physical and medical screening, outdoor physical efficiency tests, an objective-type written examination, interview and NCC certification assessment. Candidates must qualify in the required physical and medical standards before participating in outdoor tests. Only candidates who qualify the PET will be called for the written examination.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Physical Standard Test 2026
content_sections.text: The notification prescribes different minimum height and chest measurements for male and female candidates. Candidates who do not meet the physical requirements may be disqualified during the recruitment process.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Physical Efficiency Test 2026
content_sections.text: The Physical Efficiency Test carries 45 marks and includes running, pull-ups, high jump and long jump. Male and female candidates have separate qualifying standards. Disqualification: Male candidates taking longer than 12 minutes 30 seconds and female candidates taking longer than 12 minutes will be disqualified. Nagaland Police Constable Syllabus 2026 Male candidates completing fewer than six pull-ups and female candidates completing fewer than three pull-ups will be disqualified. A maximum of three attempts is permitted. Candidates who fail to meet the required qualifying standard in any of the outdoor tests will not be permitted to continue in the recruitment process.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Written Exam Pattern 2026
content_sections.text: The Nagaland Police Constable written examination will consist of 80 multiple-choice questions carrying 40 marks. Candidates will receive two hours to complete the question paper, which will be set in English.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Written Exam Syllabus 2026
content_sections.text: The written examination may cover the following subjects and knowledge areas specified in the official notification: General Awareness and General Knowledge General Science Indian History Indian Polity Social Sciences Elementary Mathematics Sports Naga Culture and Heritage Nagaland State and Naga Tribes General Mental Aptitude

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Interview and NCC Marks 2026
content_sections.text: After the PET and written examination, candidates will be shortlisted for interview based on the aggregate marks obtained in these two stages. The shortlisting ratio is three candidates for each available post. The interview carries 10 marks, and NCC certification may contribute up to 5 additional marks to the overall merit assessment.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Medical Fitness Requirements
content_sections.text: Candidates must satisfy the medical fitness standards prescribed for police service. Medical examination includes assessment of height, weight, chest, vision, hearing and physical fitness. The notification identifies several disqualifying conditions, including: Eyesight below the prescribed standard. Colour blindness. Deafness or serious hearing impairment. Varicose veins. Squint eyes. Amputated limbs or physical extremities. Physical deformities, including flat feet and knocked knees. Adverse drug screening or alcohol abuse test findings. Candidates must also satisfy the medical and physical requirements during the recruitment process and subsequent training.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply Online for Nagaland Police Constable Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Eligible applicants must submit their applications through the Nagaland Police Registration Portal between 31 October and 30 November 2026. Offline applications will not be accepted. Important: Applicants must submit only through the official online recruitment portal. Applications submitted to police offices or other establishments will not be accepted.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Documents Required 2026
content_sections.text: Original documents must be produced whenever required during the recruitment process. Applicants should ensure that the details submitted online match their supporting certificates.

content_sections.heading: Nagaland Police Constable Probation and Posting
content_sections.text: Selected candidates will undergo a probation period of two years. Service confirmation will depend on satisfactory completion of probation, medical clearance and verification of antecedents under the applicable rules. Fresh recruits will initially be deployed in India Reserve (IR) Battalions and may be required to serve within or outside Nagaland according to the instructions of the Nagaland Police Department.

basic_details.job_title: IOCL Apprentice Recruitment 2026 – Apply Online for 500 Technician Apprentice, Trade Apprentice and More Posts
basic_details.short_information: Indian Oil Corporation Limited (Pipelines Division), a Government of India Undertaking, has invited applications for around 500 apprentices across seven trades: Technician Apprentice (Mechanical, Electrical, Telecommunication & Instrumentation), Trade Apprentice (Assistant-Human Resource, Accountant), Data Entry Operator (Fresher Apprentices) and Domestic Data Entry Operator (Skill Certificate Holders). The stipend is as prescribed under the Apprentices Act and the Corporation's guidelines, and the training lasts 12 months. Candidates apply on the NATS or NAPS portal and then on the Indian Oil

Technician Apprentice (Electrical) Three years (or lateral entry after Class-XII (Sc)/ITI admitted in 2nd year of Diploma course) full time Diploma in Electrical Engineering or Electrical & Electronics Engineering. Technician Apprentice (Telecommunication & Instrumentation) Three years (or lateral entry after Class-XII (Sc)/ITI admitted in 2nd year of Diploma course) full time Diploma in any of the disciplines of Engineering listed below the table, from a Govt. recognized Institute. Trade Apprentice (Assistant-Human Resource) Full Time Bachelor degree (Graduation) from a Govt. recognized Institute/University. Trade Apprentice (Accountant) Full Time Bachelor degree (Graduation) in Commerce from a Govt. recognized Institute/University. Data Entry Operator (Fresher Apprentices) Minimum 12th Pass (but below Graduate). Domestic Data Entry Operator (Skill Certificate Holders) Minimum 12th Pass (but below Graduate), and a Skill Certificate of 'Domestic Data Entry Operator' for training of less than one year, issued by an awarding body recognized under National Skill Qualifications Framework or any other authority recognized by the Central Govt. | Disciplines accepted for Technician Apprentice (Telecommunication & Instrumentation): | Electronics & Communication Engineering Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering Electronics & Radio Communication Engineering Instrumentation & Control Engineering Instrumentation & Process Control Engineering Electronics Engineering | The qualification must already be passed on 30.11.2026, the date for reckoning eligibility. Candidates whose result is awaited on that date are not eligible. The disability certificate must be in terms of Rule 18(1) and 20 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules, 2017, in Form V, VI or VII. | Trade Suitable disabilities Technician Apprentice (Mechanical/Electrical/Telecommunication & Instrumentation) Leprosy cured, Dwarfism

salary_details.details: The apprenticeship lasts 12 months from the date of engagement. The monthly stipend is as prescribed under the Apprentices Act, 1961/1973, the Apprentices Rules 1992/2019 as amended from time to time, and the Corporation's guidelines. During the apprenticeship no other monetary or non-monetary benefit such as accommodation, HRA, conveyance or medical facility is admissible; apprentices arrange these themselves. The terms of engagement are governed by The Apprentices Act, 1961 and Rules 1992 as amended. On completion, the Corporation has no obligation to offer employment, and an apprentice cannot claim employment on that ground.

selection_process: Selection is by a Panel cum Merit List
followed by document verification and medical fitness. There is no written test or personal interview.

All applicants for a post who meet the eligibility criteria are ranked in descending order of the percentage of marks (aggregate of all subjects of all years/semesters) in the essential qualification for the trade applied. Where CGPA/OGPA or letter grade is awarded

the equivalent aggregate percentage must be entered in the application. A certificate from the Board/University/Institute stating the equivalent percentage must be uploaded and produced at document verification
otherwise candidature is not considered. If the Board does not follow a conversion formula
a certificate to that effect is needed
and the aggregate grade score of each semester/year divided by the number of semesters/years is considered. Ties go to the older candidate
and if the date of birth is also the same
to the higher Matriculation percentage. Candidates are shortlisted purely on the information furnished in the online portal.

The list of candidates provisionally selected for Document Verification and Medical Fitness will be published on the IOCL website. Candidates receive a link on their registered email to give their preference for the place of document verification and three preferences for the place of apprenticeship training in the applied State (wherever applicable). Allotment of the training place is based on merit. Originals are verified before joining
and an offer of engagement is issued only to candidates whose documents
including the medical fitness certificate
are in order.
how_to_apply: Applying is a two-portal process. The NAPS/NATS application must come first, before registering on the Indian Oil Pipelines portal. No other mode of application is accepted.

Register as an apprentice on the portal for your trade: https://www.apprenticeshipindia.gov.in (NAPS) for Data Entry Operator (Fresher Apprentices) and Domestic Data Entry Operator (Skill Certificate Holders); https://nats.education.gov.in/student_register.php (NATS) for the three Technician Apprentice trades and for Trade Apprentice (Assistant-Human Resource/Accountant).

Log in with your User ID/Email ID and apply for the opening with the Establishment ID of IOCL for your region, between 06.11.2026 and 05.12.2026. Check that your personal details, educational details, category and aggregate percentage show correctly; corrections are made through the NAPS/NATS office.
Register on the Indian Oil Pipelines portal https://plapps.indianoilpipelines.in/ using the same email ID and mobile number as on NAPS/NATS; both must stay valid for the whole apprenticeship period.
In Part-I, enter basic details such as name and category and create a password. A registration number is sent to your email ID/SMS; log in again with it and your password.

In Part-II, upload a scanned colour photograph (20-50 KB, JPG) and signature in black ink (10-30 KB, JPG), enter educational qualification and experience details, and submit. This is the final submission and details cannot be changed afterwards.
Mention the NAPS/NATS registration/enrolment number in the Indian Oil Pipelines portal, and complete this application by 05.12.2026.
Take a printout of the filled-in online application.
The portal also hosts FAQs/How to apply options, and the disability certificate format, caste/tribe/EWS certificate formats and the pre-engagement medical guidelines are under its Downloads section.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Applications are invited from eligible Indian Nationals. Candidates select their trade on the basis of their qualification at the time of application, and can apply for one Trade Code only. Disciplines accepted for Technician Apprentice (Telecommunication & Instrumentation): Electronics & Communication Engineering Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering Electronics & Radio Communication Engineering Instrumentation & Control Engineering Instrumentation & Process Control Engineering Electronics Engineering The qualification must already be passed on 30.11.2026, the date for reckoning eligibility. Candidates whose result is awaited on that date are not eligible. The Graduate/Diploma qualification must be a regular full-time course in the relevant trade/discipline from a recognized University/Institute, with minimum 50% aggregate marks (45% for SC/ST and PwBD candidates for the posts reserved for them). The notice also lists the PwBD categories (minimum 40% disability) for which each trade is suitable. The disability certificate must be in terms of Rule 18(1) and 20 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules, 2017, in Form V, VI or VII. Minimum 18 years and maximum 24 years as on 30.11.2026, which is the date for reckoning any eligibility criteria. The upper age limit is relaxed as follows. Candidates whose qualification was acquired through part-time, correspondence or distance education. Candidates with higher professional qualifications such as BE/B.Tech., MBA, CA, LLB, MCA or equivalent, or pursuing a higher qualification and having completed it on or before joining apprenticeship training. Candidates who have undergone apprenticeship training earlier or are pursuing it under the Apprentices Act. Candidates with training and/or job experience of one year or more after attaining the qualification. Candidates who have completed five years after acquiring the prescribed qualification as on 30.11.2026. Candidates applying for more than one Trade Code; such applications will be summarily rejected. Reservation of seats to SC/ST/OBC (Non Creamy Layer)/PwBD/EWS candidates is as per the applicable Govt. guidelines. The minimum qualification marks are relaxed by 5% for SC/ST/PwBD candidates considered against reserved positions. If EWS seats in a trade cannot be filled from EWS candidates, they may be filled by unreserved category candidates on the basis of position in the Panel cum Merit List. SC/ST/OBC (NCL) candidates applying for an Unreserved seat are considered on the standards applicable to General category candidates. For OBC (NCL), the caste named in the certificate must be in the Central List of OBCs of the respective State, and the Non-Creamy Layer status must be valid on the cut-off date. Candidates should refer to the official notification for the discipline-specific eligibility of each trade.

faq.answer: The notice invites applications for around 500 apprentices in the IOCL Pipelines Division, with the seats described as tentative. The break-up is ERPL 116, WRPL 149, NRPL 110, SRPL 46 and SERPL 79.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for the IOCL apprentice posts?
faq.answer: The last date for submission of the online application is 5 December 2026. Applications opened on 6 November 2026, and the same dates apply on the NATS/NAPS portal and the Indian Oil Pipelines portal.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for IOCL apprentice 2026?
faq.answer: It depends on the trade: a full-time diploma in the listed engineering disciplines for Technician Apprentice, a full-time Bachelor degree for Trade Apprentice (Commerce for Accountant), and minimum 12th pass but below graduate for the Data Entry Operator posts. The qualification must be passed by 30.11.2026.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for the IOCL apprentice recruitment?
faq.answer: The age must be minimum 18 years and maximum 24 years as on 30.11.2026. The upper limit is relaxed by up to 5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC (NCL) and 10 years for PwBD candidates.

faq.question: Q5. How do I apply for IOCL Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: First register and apply on NAPS (Data Entry Operator posts) or NATS (all other trades) using the IOCL Establishment ID of your region. Then complete Part-I and Part-II registration on https://plapps.indianoilpipelines.in/ by 05.12.2026.

faq.question: Q6. Is there a written test or interview for the IOCL apprentice posts?
faq.answer: No. The notice says there shall be no written test or personal interview. Selection is by a Panel cum Merit List based on the percentage of marks in the essential qualification, followed by document verification and medical fitness.

faq.question: Q7. How long is the IOCL apprenticeship and is it a permanent job?
faq.answer: The training lasts 12 months from the date of engagement under The Apprentices Act, 1961. It is not a permanent job: the Corporation has no obligation to offer employment after the apprenticeship.

faq.question: Q8. Will IOCL apprentices get HRA or accommodation?
faq.answer: No. Apart from the monthly stipend, no other monetary or non-monetary benefit such as accommodation, HRA, conveyance or medical facility is admissible. Apprentices make their own arrangements.

faq.question: Q9. Can I apply for more than one trade?
faq.answer: No. A candidate can apply for one Trade Code only, and applicants for more than one Trade Code will not be considered and their applications will be summarily rejected.

faq.question: Q10. Who is not eligible for the IOCL apprentice posts?
faq.answer: Candidates who have done apprenticeship training before, have one year or more of training or job experience after the qualification, or finished the qualification more than five years before 30.11.2026 are not eligible. Candidates with part-time or distance qualifications or higher professional qualifications are also excluded.

content_sections.heading: OSSSC Ophthalmic Officer Recruitment 2026 Notification PDF
content_sections.text: The Odisha Sub-ordinate Staff Selection Commission has issued the for recruitment of 238 District Cadre Group-C Ophthalmic Officers. The detailed 15-page notification contains district-wise vacancies, reservation, educational qualifications, professional registration, age limit, salary, examination fee, written-test pattern, negative marking, merit rules and online application instructions. Official Detailed Notification:

content_sections.heading: OSSSC Ophthalmic Officer Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Candidates must have passed +2 Science or its equivalent and successfully completed the prescribed two-year certified ophthalmic training programme. Valid registration with the Ophthalmic Officers' Council in Odisha is also mandatory. Yes. The notification requires a two-year certified Ophthalmic Assistant Training Course or certified Ophthalmic Surgical Assistant Course from a Government or Government-recognized institution of Odisha. Candidates who have passed +2 Science but do not possess the prescribed professional training qualification are not eligible. Yes. Candidates must have registered their names with the Ophthalmic Officers' Council in Odisha and possess a valid registration certificate when submitting the online application form. The registration certificate must be uploaded as required by the application portal. Candidates should not assume they can obtain the mandatory registration only after the recruitment examination. Candidates must be able to read, write and speak Odia and must satisfy at least one of the prescribed language-related qualification conditions. Passed the Middle School Examination with Odia as a language subject. Passed Matriculation or equivalent with Odia as the medium of examination in non-language subjects. Passed Odia as a language subject in the final examination of Class VII from a recognized institution. Passed the prescribed Odia language test at M.E. School standard conducted by the competent authority. Important: Knowing conversational Odia alone does not replace the required supporting language qualification or certificate. Candidates must be Indian citizens, possess good character and satisfy the marriage-related and other eligibility conditions prescribed under the relevant Odisha Government service rules.

content_sections.heading: OSSSC Ophthalmic Officer Exam Pattern 2026

Meeting the minimum qualifying marks does not guarantee selection. Final shortlisting depends on examination performance, category-wise merit and the number of vacancies. If two or more candidates obtain equal written examination scores, the commission will apply the prescribed tie-breaking criteria. Higher percentage marks in the qualifying Ophthalmic Assistant or Ophthalmic Surgical Assistant examination. Higher age, where the professional qualification percentage is also equal. Higher Class 12 examination marks, if the tie continues. Other criteria determined by the commission where the preceding stages do not resolve the tie.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply Online for OSSSC Ophthalmic Officer Recruitment 2026?
content_sections.text: Visit the official website at www.osssc.gov.in . Open the Apply Online section. Select the Ophthalmic Officer Recruitment 2026 application. If you are a new user, select New User Registration . If you have registered previously for OSSSC recruitment, select the prescribed Re-registration option. Carefully complete the registration or re-registration process. Keep the generated User ID and other login credentials secure. Log in to the OSSSC applicant portal. Open the Ophthalmic Officer online application form. Enter the requested personal, educational and professional qualification details. Provide the relevant Ophthalmic Officers' Council registration information. Enter the applicable category, reservation and other eligibility details. Complete the district preference section as provided in the application form. Upload the required photograph, signature and supporting documents. Pay the applicable examination fee through the online payment gateway. Check that the payment and application confirmation have been generated. Review the application carefully and complete final submission. Save the application details for future reference. Complete registration by 29 November 2026 and final application submission by 5 December 2026 . Important: Candidates must submit a complete online application. Incomplete applications will be summarily rejected. More than one application submitted by the same candidate may also result in cancellation of the candidature.

content_sections.heading: OSSSC Ophthalmic Officer Documents Required 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates should keep their original certificates and supporting records ready for application and subsequent verification. Class 10 certificate or equivalent age proof. +2 Science certificate and marksheet. Two-year certified Ophthalmic Assistant Training Course or Ophthalmic Surgical Assistant Course certificate. Valid registration certificate from the Ophthalmic Officers' Council, Odisha. Odia language qualification certificate or prescribed language-test evidence. Valid photo identity proof. Recent passport-size photograph. Scanned signature. SC/ST/SEBC certificate, where applicable. PwD certificate or UDID card, where applicable. Ex-Servicemen discharge and service documents, where applicable. Sports qualification certificate, if claiming the applicable reservation. Appointment letters and relevant employment documents for eligible contractual Ophthalmic Assistants claiming the notified age relaxation. Other documents prescribed by the commission during verification. The photograph must be clear and recent. Candidates should keep the same photograph available throughout the recruitment process. The exact upload requirements displayed on the official application portal must be followed.

content_sections.heading: OSSSC Ophthalmic Officer District Preference and Posting 2026
content_sections.text: Ophthalmic Officer is a District Cadre post . Candidates are recruited for district establishments under the Health & Family Welfare Department. The commission will consider the district preference, merit position, applicable reservation and vacancies during the final allocation process. The commission may notify an option to revise or re-exercise district preferences before the allotment stage. If a candidate does not use the available revision facility, the district preferences already submitted may be treated as final. Candidates should monitor official recruitment notices and meet any specified preference-revision deadlines.

content_sections.heading: OSSSC Ophthalmic Officer Document Verification 2026
content_sections.text: After the written examination, OSSSC will prepare a provisional merit list and shortlist eligible candidates for document verification. The commission may shortlist candidates for verification based on the number of vacancies and the applicable category-wise requirements, including a minimum shortlisting ratio of 1.25 times the notified category-wise vacancies where applicable. Original qualification, council registration, age, language and reservation certificates must be produced before the competent verification authority. Important: Provisional inclusion in the merit list does not guarantee appointment. Any discrepancy between the online application and original documents may lead to rejection.

content_sections.heading: OSSSC Ophthalmic Officer Admit Card 2026
content_sections.text: OSSSC will announce the written examination date and admit card availability through its official website. Eligible candidates must download their admission letter using the designated applicant login or admission-letter facility. The commission will not send admission letters by post. Applicants should regularly check official notices, their registered mobile number and their email account.

content_sections.heading: AP DSC Notification 2026: Three Official Notifications
content_sections.text: Do not treat all 2,721 posts as one teacher category. The recruitment has three separate notifications with different managements, qualifications and selection provisions.

content_sections.heading: AP DSC Vacancy 2026 Post-Wise
content_sections.text: Secondary Grade Teacher is the largest individual category with 1,205 regular posts. The table below also identifies special education and residential-school vacancies separately.

content_sections.heading: AP DSC 2026 District-Wise Vacancies
content_sections.text: The 26-district breakup below covers 2,461 regular and special education posts . Society vacancies (260 posts) are counted separately, not added to any district in this table. Kurnool has 404 posts, followed by Prakasam (291) and YSR Kadapa (227).

content_sections.heading: AP DSC Societies Vacancies 2026
content_sections.text: These posts are under residential education societies, model schools and the Welfare of Differently Abled, Transgender and Senior Citizens Department. The vacancy distribution varies by society and cadre.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply for AP DSC 2026? Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Educational qualifications are post-specific and governed by the relevant recruitment rules and Information Bulletin. Applicants should not assume that qualification for SGT also qualifies them for SA, TGT, PGT, Principal, PD, PET or Special Education posts. Check the appropriate bulletin for the required academic degree, professional teacher-training qualification, subject or medium, TET eligibility where applicable, and any special education recognition requirements. The notifications direct candidates to the Information Bulletin for the complete post-wise qualifications. Applicants must meet the prescribed qualifications by the applicable notification cutoff; check the relevant bulletin before paying the fee.

content_sections.heading: AP DSC Age Limit 2026
content_sections.text: Age is calculated as on 1 July 2026 . The detailed notifications provide an ordinary upper limit of 44 years, with higher limits for specified reserved categories.

rows.age_limit: Relaxation as provided in the relevant recruitment notification

content_sections.heading: AP DSC Application Fee 2026
content_sections.text: The application fee is ₹1,000 for each post . Candidates applying for more than one post should check the relevant application instructions and the total payable amount before submitting payment. The official payment window runs from 11 to 30 November 2026.

content_sections.heading: AP DSC Selection Process and Minimum Qualifying Marks
content_sections.text: The selection method depends on the post. The regular SA (except Physical Education) and SGT notifications specify aggregate TRT (80%) and qualifying TET (20%) marks. The societies notification specifies TRT (80%) and TET (20%) for TGT, while Principal, PGT, PD and PET qualifying marks are based on TRT (100%). Do not apply the same weightage mechanically to every post. These are minimum qualifying thresholds, not guaranteed selection cutoffs. The societies notification also provides an English Language Proficiency screening test for Principal, non-language PGT and non-language TGT candidates: 60/100 marks for OC, BC and EWS; 50/100 for SC, ST, PwBD and ex-servicemen. The notification excludes TGT Special Education (Special Schools) from this English screening test. The Special Education notification separately provides certain eligible service candidates with service weightage of 0.5 marks per completed year, up to 5 marks , subject to the stated conditions and overall maximum. Candidates must refer to that notification for eligible service categories and proof requirements. Also Check: AP DSC Syllabus 2026

content_sections.heading: AP DSC Syllabus 2026 and Exam Pattern
content_sections.text: The Government of Andhra Pradesh has released a detailed suggestive syllabus covering SGT, SGT Special Education, School Assistants, TGT, TGT Special Education, PGT, Principals and Physical Education posts. Candidates should prepare using the syllabus for their exact post and subject; the department states that the topics are indicative rather than exhaustive. The official syllabus also includes separate subject coverage for School Assistant languages, Mathematics, Physical Science, Biological Science and Social Studies; distinct TGT and PGT papers; English proficiency where applicable; Principals; PET; and SA-PE/PD. Open the official syllabus PDF rather than relying on a generic common syllabus.

Visit the official portal at tet2dsc.apcfss.in . Read the correct detailed notification and Information Bulletin for the post. Check your qualifications, age, TET requirements and district or management eligibility. From 11 November, follow the registration and application steps shown in the official User Guide. Review all details carefully and pay the prescribed ₹1,000 fee per post. Complete the final submission by 30 November 2026 and retain the application confirmation for future reference.

content_sections.heading: About BSF
content_sections.text: The Border Security Force is a Central Armed Police Force under the Ministry of Home Affairs. This circular was issued by its Medical Directorate at the Directorate General, Block-9, Level-4, East Block, Sector-1, R K Puram, New Delhi - 110066, and signed by Dr. Umesh Tiwari, Inspector General/Director(Medical). The posts are in the BSF Medical Set-up, which the subject line calls the BSF paramedical set-up.

content_sections.heading: Where and How to Send
content_sections.text: Nominations of eligible and willing candidates go in the enclosed proforma to this address: Inspector General/Director(Medical), Directorate General, BSF, Block No. 9, Level-04, East Block, Sector-1, R K Puram, New Delhi-110066. Fill in the Bio-Data proforma (page 5 of the circular) and paste a photograph in the space provided. Sign the proforma, write your address, and get it counter-signed by your Head of Office (HOO) with seal. Get the "Certificate to be furnished by the Employer/Head of Office/Forwarding Authority" (page 6) completed and signed by the HOO with the official seal. Attach duly attested copies of your CR dossiers/APARs for the last five years, attested on each page. Your department forwards the nomination to the address above, so that it reaches BSF by the 60th day from publication in the Employment News. Applications received directly from candidates will not be entertained. The notice does not mention what to write on the envelope or a particular postal mode.

content_sections.heading: Posts, Eligibility and Pay
content_sections.text: The notice does not give a category-wise break-up of the vacancies. Officers of the Central Armed Police Forces or the Central Government or the State Government or the Union territory administration, (a) (i) holding an analogous post on regular basis in the parent cadre or department; or (ii) with six years regular service in Level-5 (Rs. 29200-92300) in the pay-matrix in the parent cadre or department; and (b) possessing the educational qualifications and experience given below for the post; and (c) shall be medically fit. Basic Nursing Assistant or Medic Course; Advance Nursing Assistant or Advance Medic Course; and Experience of minimum six years as Nursing Assistant in a hundred bedded Hospital or institute recognised by the Central Government or a State Government or Central Armed Police Forces Hospitals. 12th Class passed from a recognised Board; and Diploma in Medical Laboratory Technician or Technology of two years duration from an institution recognised by the Central Government or a State Government; and Experience of minimum six years as Laboratory Technician from a Laboratory Diagnostic Centre or minimum hundred bedded hospital or an institution recognised by the Central Government or a State Government. 12th Class passed from a recognised Board; and Diploma in Physiotherapy of two years duration from an institute recognised by the Central Government or a State Government; and Experience of minimum six years as Physiotherapist from a Physiotherapy Centre or minimum hundred bedded Hospital or Institute recognised by the Central Government or the State Government. Preference will be given to those with a certificate or diploma in the trade from a recognized Institute. Departmental officers in the feeder category who are in the direct line of promotion shall not be eligible for appointment on deputation. Deputationists shall not be eligible for consideration for appointment by promotion. For all three posts, the maximum age limit for appointment by deputation shall not exceed 56 years (fifty-six years) as on the closing date of receipt of applications. The notice lists no age relaxation. The crucial date for determining eligibility is the last date prescribed for receipt of nominations, in accordance with DoP&T OM No. AB-14017/71/89-Estt.RR dated 03.10.1989. Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions of each post.

content_sections.heading: Terms of Deputation
content_sections.text: The period of deputation in the BSF Medical Set-up shall ordinarily not exceed three years. This period includes any deputation in another ex-cadre post held immediately before this appointment, in the same or another organisation or department of the Central Government. Selected candidates are governed by DOP&T OM No. 6/8/2009-Estt.(Pay II) dated 17.06.2010 and MHA (Police-II Division) L/No. I-21022/03/2016-Pers-II dated 22.11.2016, as amended from time to time. Deputation gives no right to claim seniority, pay and allowances or any other pecuniary or service benefits over others. Seniority continues to be counted in the original cadre/department for all purposes, including promotion and financial up-gradation. Deputationists have no inherent right to claim absorption, because the discretion to absorb them rests solely with the BSF. BSF may return a deputationist early to the parent cadre for unsuitability, indiscipline, exigency of service or other unforeseen factors. This requires three months' advance notice to the lending Ministry/Department and the employee.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: Bio-Data proforma with photograph, signed by the candidate and counter-signed by HOO with seal Photocopy of the Diploma/Degree in the respective trade Photocopy of the SC/ST certificate, if the candidate belongs to SC/ST Duly attested copies of CR dossiers/APARs for the last five years (attested on each page) Copy of the health card, with the medical category certified by the HOO Certificate from the Employer/Head of Office/Forwarding Authority A separate sheet for additional information, if the space in the form is insufficient The Bio-Data form asks for the name, date of birth, educational qualifications, and employment details in chronological order (office, post held, period, scale of pay and basic pay, nature of duties). It also asks for the present pay with next increment, penalties if any, training programmes attended, and the nature of present employment. For candidates already on deputation or contract, it asks for deputation/contract details, any revised scale of pay, and total emoluments per month now drawn. In the employer certificate, the HOO confirms the following: The particulars furnished are correct. No disciplinary or vigilance case is pending or contemplated against the candidate. The candidate's integrity is beyond doubt. No major or minor penalties have been imposed on the candidate during the last 10 years. The candidate will be relieved to join on selection.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: For candidates posted in BSF under-command Units/SHQrs, the circular directs the BSF Frontier HQrs, Training Institutions and Composite Hospitals to assemble a Departmental Screening Committee (DSC). The DSC assesses and selects candidates as per existing instructions/RRs and sends its proceedings to the Directorate. The notice does not describe the selection method for nominations from other organisations.

content_sections.heading: About District Programme Officer, ICDS, Ballia
content_sections.text: The District Programme Officer, ICDS, Ballia runs the Integrated Child Development Services in Ballia district of Uttar Pradesh through 18 child development projects (Bal Vikas Pariyojana). This recruitment is being held under Government Order No. 1/1092245/2025/3313/58-1-2025(1917687) dated 17 September 2025, with the approval of the District Magistrate dated 3 November 2026.

content_sections.heading: Ballia Anganwadi Worker Vacancy Details 2026
content_sections.text: The notice prints a total of 242 vacancies. These are the project-wise figures it gives, with the category break-up for each project (UR = Unreserved, OBC = Other Backward Class, SC = Scheduled Caste, ST = Scheduled Tribe). The notice also attaches centre-wise lists signed by the Child Development Project Officers of Bairia, Bansdih, Belhari, Beruarbari, City, Chilkahar, Dubhad, Garwar and Hanumanganj. These lists give each vacant Anganwadi centre, its gram panchayat or ward, its unique code and its reserved category. The complete gram sabha and ward-wise details, with reservation, are posted on the notice boards of the Collectorate, Vikas Bhawan, Tehsil and Block offices, and are uploaded on upanganwadibharti.in. The notice warns that the number of posts may go up or down.

content_sections.heading: Ballia Anganwadi Worker Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: The minimum age is 18 years and the maximum is 35 years. A candidate must be 18 years old on 1 July 2026. Only the date of birth recorded in the High School marksheet and certificate is accepted. The minimum educational qualification is Intermediate or equivalent. The merit list is prepared on the basis of educational qualification up to a maximum of Postgraduate. Only women candidates are eligible. Two women from one family will not be appointed at the same Anganwadi centre. Residence and caste certificates are valid only if the Tehsil has issued them online with a digital signature and they can be verified online. The income certificate must be issued by the competent authority under Revenue Section-9 Government Order No. 3959/1-9-11-Raj-9 dated 30 September 2011 (as amended). It must be verifiable online and must have been issued within three years before 26 November 2026. Income, caste and residence certificates issued after 26 November 2026 will not be accepted. Check the official notification and the centre-wise lists for the category and location of each vacancy.

content_sections.heading: Ballia Anganwadi Worker Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: Selection follows the Government Order dated 17 September 2025. Merit is based on educational qualification. For each centre, candidates are considered in this order of preference: Widowed, legally divorced or abandoned women from below-poverty-line (BPL) families who live in the same gram sabha, or in the same ward in urban areas. If there are none, BPL women from the same gram sabha or ward. If there are none, widowed, legally divorced or abandoned women from above-poverty-line (APL) families of the same gram sabha or ward. If there are none, women from APL families of the same gram sabha or ward. If no eligible candidate in any of these groups is found in the gram sabha, selection is made category-wise from the concerned Nyay Panchayat in the same order. A widow must provide a death certificate issued by the Gram Panchayat Officer or the urban local body, along with a certified copy of the family register. A divorced or abandoned woman must provide a legal order issued by a court. The BPL income limit for rural and urban areas follows Social Welfare Section-2 Government Order No. 22/2015/2123/26-2-2015 dated 14 September 2015 (as amended). The selection committee or appointing authority has the power to cancel any selection.

A merit list follows. The preliminary examination has 100 objective multiple-choice questions at matric level. It carries 400 marks (4 marks per question) and lasts two hours. One mark is deducted for each wrong answer. The medium is Hindi/English, and if the Hindi and English papers differ, the English questions are treated as correct. Candidates must obtain these qualifying marks in the preliminary examination, or they will be out of the competition: If many applications are received, the examination may be held in more than one phase. In that case, results will be prepared after normalisation. The FAQ on equating of scores linked in the notice ( http://vidhansabha.bih.nic.in/pdf/recruitment/FAQ.pdf ) explains the process. General Studies: current affairs (national and international events, scientific progress, awards, sports and players). Also India and its neighbouring countries: history of neighbouring countries; history, culture, geography, economic scene, agriculture and natural resources of India and Bihar; the Constitution and political system of India; Panchayati Raj; community development; Five-Year Plans; the freedom movement and Bihar's contribution to it. Questions may focus on Bihar, India and neighbouring countries. General Science and Mathematics: mainly matric level. Physics, Chemistry and Biology; number system, computation of whole numbers, decimals and fractions, relationship between numbers, fundamental arithmetical operations, percentage, ratio and proportion, average, interest, and profit and loss. Mental Ability and Logical Reasoning: verbal and non-verbal questions on analogies, similarities and differences, space visualisation, problem solving, analysis, visual memory, discrimination, observation, relationship concepts, arithmetical reasoning, arithmetic number series, and coding and decoding. The preliminary results will be declared for the typing test. Candidates who obtain the qualifying marks are called for the typing test, in a number approximately 10 times the total vacancies. A speed of 30 words per minute each in Hindi and English typing is desirable. Each test lasts 10 minutes, with a 1.5% relaxation for typing mistakes. The test is held on a computer, and the Hindi typing test is taken in the Kruti Dev font. A merit list will be published from the candidates who pass the preliminary examination and are found fit in the typing test, to fill the category-wise vacancies. If one post is contested between two candidates, the desirable qualification prescribed for the post is used to decide. These qualifications are given in the schedule to the Bihar Vidhan Sabha Sachivalaya (Recruitment and Service Conditions) Rules, 2018. content_sections.heading: HCI Job Description
content_sections.text: Manager (Purchase) Report to the Head of MMD/In-charge MMD, HCI. Responsible for ensuring that all required items are sourced and no wastage or stock-out situation arises as per laid out SOPs. Ensure that the items reach the user department timely as per the prescribed quality and standard. Adhere to the Company Purchase Manual, GFR (General Financial Rules), CVC Guidelines, MSE/Make in India norms and Audit readiness (Internal/Statutory /CAG). Experience in procurement of materials, preparation of purchase requisitions, vendor management, comparative statement preparation, negotiation, and purchase order management. Junior Sous Chef Reporting to the Executive Chef. Responsible for preparing the dishes as per laid-out SOPs and on a timely basis as per the day’s schedule and menu. Commis-I (Indian) Reporting to the Sous Chef. Responsible for preparing the dishes as per laid-out SOPs and on a timely basis as per the day’s schedule and menu. Commis-I (Bakery & Confectionery) Reporting to the Sous Chef. Responsible for preparing the dishes as per laid-out SOPs and on a timely basis as per the day’s schedule and menu. Associate-Engineering (AC & Refrigeration/ Electrician/ Plumber) Reporting to HOD -Maintenance. Responsible for the upkeep, routine repairs & maintenance as well as ensuring preventive maintenance of all the items installed/ placed in the hotel, including Kitchen Appliances, Air-conditioning, Plumbing, Lighting, etc.

content_sections.heading: RRB NTPC Undergraduate Recruitment 2026 Important Dates
content_sections.text: The RRB NTPC 12th Pass application process starts on 15 October 2026. Candidates must submit the online form by 13 November, while the examination fee can be paid until 15 November 2026. A separate correction window is available after the application closing date. RRBs will announce CBT dates, document verification and medical examination schedules through the unified official Railway Recruitment Board website.

content_sections.heading: RRB NTPC Undergraduate Vacancy 2026 Post-wise Details
content_sections.text: Railway Recruitment Boards have announced 1,688 undergraduate vacancies across four posts. Commercial cum Ticket Clerk has the highest number of vacancies at 700, followed by Junior Clerk cum Typist with 600 posts. The detailed RRB-wise, Railway Zone-wise and post-wise vacancy distribution is provided in Annexure B of the official notification on pages 33–40. Candidates should check vacancies for their preferred RRB before submitting the application.

content_sections.heading: RRB NTPC Undergraduate Eligibility Criteria 2026
content_sections.text: Applicants for RRB NTPC Undergraduate Recruitment 2026 must have passed Class 12 or an equivalent examination from a recognized board. The notification normally requires at least 50% aggregate marks, but specified candidates are exempt from this minimum-percentage condition. Qualification Cut-off: The required educational qualification must be completed by 13 November 2026. Candidates awaiting final examination results are not eligible to apply. Normally, candidates must secure at least 50% aggregate marks in Class 12. However, the minimum 50% condition is not applicable to the following candidates: Scheduled Caste candidates. Scheduled Tribe candidates. Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Ex-Servicemen. Candidates possessing qualifications higher than Class 12. Yes. Candidates with qualifications higher than Class 12 can apply for the undergraduate posts if they satisfy the prescribed age, medical and other eligibility conditions. The 50% Class 12 minimum marks condition is not insisted upon for such candidates.

content_sections.heading: RRB NTPC Undergraduate Salary 2026
content_sections.text: RRB NTPC Undergraduate posts are placed under Pay Levels 2 and 3 of the 7th Central Pay Commission. The Commercial cum Ticket Clerk post carries initial basic pay of Rs. 21,700, while the remaining three posts carry Rs. 19,900. These are initial basic pay figures, not the total monthly take-home salary.

content_sections.heading: RRB NTPC Undergraduate Application Fee 2026
content_sections.text: The RRB NTPC Undergraduate application fee is Rs. 500 for general applicants and Rs. 250 for the eligible concessional categories listed in the notification. Part or all of the examination fee is refundable, after deduction of applicable bank charges, only to candidates who appear in the first-stage CBT. Payment Methods: Internet Banking, Debit Card, Credit Card and UPI. Only candidates appearing in CBT-1 are eligible for the prescribed refund. The refund is subject to deduction of applicable bank charges. Refunds are processed to an Aadhaar-seeded bank account as provided in the notification. Candidates must ensure their bank account is correctly linked with Aadhaar. Rejected or incomplete applications do not qualify for a fee refund. Important: Economically Backward Class (EBC), Economically Weaker Section (EWS) and Other Backward Class (OBC) are different categories. EBC concession is based on the conditions specified in the notification and does not itself provide job reservation.

content_sections.heading: RRB NTPC Undergraduate Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: The recruitment process consists of two Computer Based Tests, followed by document verification and medical examination. Unlike several previous NTPC recruitment cycles, CEN 07/2026 does not require a separate Computer Based Typing Skill Test for Junior Clerk cum Typist or Accounts Clerk cum Typist. CBT-1: First-stage Computer Based Test for all four posts. CBT-2: Second-stage Computer Based Test for shortlisted candidates. Document Verification: Verification of original educational, identity, category and other required documents. Medical Examination: Candidates must pass the prescribed medical fitness standard for their allotted post. No. The Computer Based Typing Skill Test for Junior Clerk cum Typist and Accounts Clerk cum Typist has been dispensed with under CEN 07/2026. Candidates are still expected to possess basic computer and adequate typing proficiency, which may be assessed after joining.

content_sections.heading: RRB NTPC Undergraduate CBT-1 Exam Pattern 2026
content_sections.text: The RRB NTPC Undergraduate first-stage CBT contains 100 objective-type questions for 100 marks. The examination duration is 90 minutes, and one-third of a mark is deducted for every incorrect answer. Duration: 90 Minutes. Negative Marking: 1/3 mark per incorrect answer. Scribe-eligible Candidates: 120 Minutes.

content_sections.heading: RRB NTPC Undergraduate CBT-2 Exam Pattern 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates shortlisted through CBT-1 will appear for CBT-2. The second-stage CBT contains 120 questions carrying 120 marks, with a duration of 90 minutes. Duration: 90 Minutes. Negative Marking: 1/3 mark per incorrect answer. Scribe-eligible Candidates: 120 Minutes. These minimum qualifying percentages apply to the CBTs. PwBD candidates may receive the specified relaxation when the notification's conditions are met. Qualifying marks alone do not guarantee shortlisting.

content_sections.heading: RRB NTPC Undergraduate Syllabus 2026
content_sections.text: The RRB NTPC Undergraduate syllabus for CBT-1 and CBT-2 covers Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, and General Awareness. Both stages have the same broad subjects but different question distributions. Number System, Decimals and Fractions LCM and HCF Ratio and Proportion Percentages Mensuration Time and Work Time and Distance Simple and Compound Interest Profit and Loss Elementary Algebra Geometry and Trigonometry Elementary Statistics Analogies Number and Alphabetical Series Coding and Decoding Mathematical Operations Similarities and Differences Relationships and Analytical Reasoning Syllogism Venn Diagrams Puzzles and Data Sufficiency Statement and Conclusion Decision Making Maps and Graph Interpretation Current Affairs - National and International Indian History and Freedom Struggle Indian and World Geography Indian Polity and Constitution Indian Economy General Science up to Class 10 Level Sports, Art, Culture and Literature Computer Basics and Applications Science and Technology Developments Government Schemes and Programmes Environmental Issues Indian Transport Systems Important National and International Organizations

content_sections.heading: RRB NTPC Undergraduate Medical Standards 2026
content_sections.text: Each undergraduate post has a prescribed railway medical standard. Candidates must satisfy the required fitness and vision conditions for the post they select. Candidates who have undergone LASIK or another procedure to correct refractive error are not eligible for posts requiring A-3 medical standards under this notification. For B-2 and C-2 posts, eligibility is subject to the medical conditions specified in the official notification.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply Online for RRB NTPC Undergraduate Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Eligible candidates must submit only one online application through the unified official RRB website from 15 October to 13 November 2026. Candidates must carefully choose the RRB and their post preferences because important details cannot be changed later. Visit https://rrb.indianrailways.gov.in/ . Open the recruitment link for CEN No. 07/2026 - NTPC Undergraduate. Read the detailed notification, Annexure A and RRB-wise vacancy tables in Annexure B. Click Create an Account if you are a new applicant. Candidates who already created an RRB account for earlier CENs should use their existing login credentials. Register using the required personal details, active mobile number and email address. Complete Aadhaar or other permitted identity verification as directed by the application portal. Choose one Railway Recruitment Board. Enter the required personal, educational and reservation details. Select eligible posts, Railway Zones and Production Unit preferences carefully. Complete the live photograph capture as instructed by the portal. Upload the scanned signature and applicable supporting documents. Review the information and declaration carefully. Pay the prescribed examination fee using the available online payment method. Submit the application and retain the confirmation details. Important: The selected RRB and details entered during Create an Account cannot be modified later. Candidates must not submit multiple applications.

content_sections.heading: RRB NTPC Undergraduate Photo and Signature Requirements 2026
content_sections.text: The RRB application process includes live photograph capture and upload of the candidate's signature. Candidates should follow the exact instructions to avoid application rejection. The candidate's photograph must be captured live through the application system. Do not upload or photograph an existing printed photograph. Follow the portal's instructions for face positioning, lighting and identity matching. The notification also requires eligible SC/ST candidates seeking a free train travel pass to upload the prescribed community certificate in PDF format.

selection_process: Selection is based on a merit list followed by a skill test and a speed test.
For posts where CTI/ATI is required
a merit list is prepared giving priority to one-year CTI/ATI certificate holders
on the marks of their technical qualification (ITI/Diploma/Degree). If no CTI/ATI certificate holder is available

candidates with the prescribed technical qualification are selected on the marks of that qualification. If a candidate holds more than one prescribed technical certificate (such as National Trade Certificate
National Apprenticeship Certificate
degree or diploma)
the certificate/marksheet with the highest marks is used.
After the merit list is approved by the Joint Director (Training)
Regional Office Jagdalpur
candidates will be called in the ratio 1:10 for a skill test and speed test. Candidates who pass these tests and get a place in merit will be selected.
The selection list will be displayed on the institute notice board

the institute website portal and the district NIC portal. Selected candidates must accept the invitation given by telephone and complete the training work. The main-list candidate gets the chance to join within the period fixed from the date the list is displayed; after that
the next serial number in the list is offered the chance.
important_instructions: Guest Lecturers are invited as per need or for a maximum of one training session. If training work or conduct is not satisfactory, the Principal / head of institute may decide to continue or remove the Guest Lecturer after giving an opportunity of hearing. Services end automatically when the government makes a regular, transfer or contract posting on that post; if such a posting happens during the process, the process for that post ends automatically. No leave except government holidays; no claim to government service will be accepted. The applicant also affirms in the affidavit never to claim a regular post. A candidate invited by more than one institute/trade/subject who joins at one place has the selection at the others cancelled automatically. Separate applications are required for each institute/trade/subject. Incomplete, unclear or incorrect applications will be rejected without intimation. Write a correct, clear mobile number in the form; the applicant is responsible if not reachable on it. The number of posts may be reduced, increased or cancelled. In any dispute, the decision of the Joint Director, Training, Regional Office Bastar Region, Jagdalpur / committee is final and binding. Guest Lecturers engaged will be subject to the final decision in case WPS 4836/2020 filed in the High Court of Chhattisgarh.

Fill in the prescribed application format, with a self-certified photograph, and mention the institute and the post/trade applied for (Guest Lecturer / Stenographer and Secretarial Assistant (Hindi)). Absence on working days of the month leads to a deduction from the honorarium as per rules, and the honorarium is paid only when budget is available under the head fixed by the government.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: Self-attested copy of the marksheet of the educational qualification Self-attested copy of the technical qualification certificate Self-attested ATI/CTI certificate (where held) Self-attested domicile (residence) certificate Self-attested copies of other qualification certificates on which the application is based Affidavit (shapath patra) on plain paper, in the format attached to the application form Self-certified photograph on the application form

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection is based on a merit list followed by a skill test and a speed test. For posts where CTI/ATI is required, a merit list is prepared giving priority to one-year CTI/ATI certificate holders, on the marks of their technical qualification (ITI/Diploma/Degree). If no CTI/ATI certificate holder is available, candidates with the prescribed technical qualification are selected on the marks of that qualification. If a candidate holds more than one prescribed technical certificate (such as National Trade Certificate, National Apprenticeship Certificate, degree or diploma), the certificate/marksheet with the highest marks is used. After the merit list is approved by the Joint Director (Training), Regional Office Jagdalpur, candidates will be called in the ratio 1:10 for a skill test and speed test. Candidates who pass these tests and get a place in merit will be selected. The selection list will be displayed on the institute notice board, the institute website portal and the district NIC portal. Selected candidates must accept the invitation given by telephone and complete the training work. The main-list candidate gets the chance to join within the period fixed from the date the list is displayed; after that, the next serial number in the list is offered the chance.

content_sections.heading: Important Instructions
content_sections.text: Guest Lecturers are invited as per need or for a maximum of one training session. If training work or conduct is not satisfactory, the Principal / head of institute may decide to continue or remove the Guest Lecturer after giving an opportunity of hearing. Services end automatically when the government makes a regular, transfer or contract posting on that post; if such a posting happens during the process, the process for that post ends automatically. No leave except government holidays; no claim to government service will be accepted. The applicant also affirms in the affidavit never to claim a regular post. A candidate invited by more than one institute/trade/subject who joins at one place has the selection at the others cancelled automatically. Separate applications are required for each institute/trade/subject. Incomplete, unclear or incorrect applications will be rejected without intimation. Write a correct, clear mobile number in the form; the applicant is responsible if not reachable on it. The number of posts may be reduced, increased or cancelled. In any dispute, the decision of the Joint Director, Training, Regional Office Bastar Region, Jagdalpur / committee is final and binding. Guest Lecturers engaged will be subject to the final decision in case WPS 4836/2020 filed in the High Court of Chhattisgarh.

content_sections.heading: Indian Army TES 57 Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: The Indian Army has announced 90 provisional vacancies for the 10+2 Technical Entry Scheme - 57. Selected candidates will undergo engineering and military training before being considered for Permanent Commission in the Army. The number of vacancies is subject to change based on the training capacity of Cadets Training Wings and the Indian Army's requirements.

content_sections.heading: Indian Army TES 57 Eligibility Criteria 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates applying for Indian Army TES 57 Recruitment 2026 must have passed Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, secured at least 60% aggregate marks in these three subjects and appeared in JEE Main 2026. The entry is open to unmarried male candidates who satisfy the prescribed nationality, age and medical standards. Must have passed Class 12 or an equivalent examination from a recognized education board. Must have studied Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (PCM). Must have secured a minimum aggregate of 60% marks in PCM. The PCM percentage is calculated using Class 12 marks in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics. Must have appeared in JEE Main 2026. Yes. Appearing in JEE Main 2026 is mandatory for TES-57. The Indian Army will shortlist eligible applicants using the JEE Main 2026 Common Rank List (CRL). Meeting the Class 12 PCM percentage requirement alone does not guarantee an SSB interview call. The 60% requirement applies to the aggregate marks obtained in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics in Class 12. Candidates must enter their actual PCM percentage up to two decimal places without rounding it off. The notification allows unmarried male candidates who satisfy the prescribed nationality requirements, including: Citizens of India. Subjects of Nepal. Eligible persons of Indian origin who migrated from the countries listed in the notification with the intention of permanently settling in India. Certain candidates require a Government of India eligibility certificate. The notification provides an exemption from this certificate requirement for Gorkha subjects of Nepal. The entry is restricted to unmarried male candidates. Selected candidates must undertake not to marry until they complete the training programme. A candidate who marries after applying will not be selected for training, even if successful in the selection process. Marriage during training can lead to discharge and recovery of the prescribed training expenditure.

content_sections.heading: Indian Army TES 57 Age Limit 2026
content_sections.text: The age limit for Indian Army TES 57 Recruitment 2026 is 16 years 6 months to 19 years 6 months as on 1 July 2027. Candidates must have been born between 1 January 2008 and 1 January 2011, with both dates included. Age Proof: The date of birth recorded in the Matriculation or Class 10 certificate, or the accepted equivalent certificate, will be used. Changes to the recorded date of birth are not permitted.

content_sections.heading: Indian Army TES 57 Selection Process 2026
content_sections.text: Selection for Indian Army TES 57 begins with shortlisting based on JEE Main 2026 CRL, followed by the Services Selection Board (SSB) interview, medical examination and final merit list. The final merit list is based on SSB marks, subject to medical fitness, eligibility and vacancy availability. Application Shortlisting: The Indian Army will shortlist applicants based on JEE Main 2026 Common Rank List and the prescribed cut-off. SSB Interview: Shortlisted candidates will undergo a five-day SSB assessment. Medical Examination: Candidates recommended by the SSB will undergo a medical examination at a military hospital. Final Merit List: Merit will be prepared based on marks obtained in the SSB interview. Joining Letter: Medically fit candidates will receive joining instructions according to merit, eligibility and available vacancies. The TES-57 SSB interviews are tentatively expected between February and March 2027. The SSB assessment is conducted over five days and consists of two stages. Candidates who do not clear Stage I are sent back on the same day. The SSB assessment includes evaluation by psychologists, Group Testing Officers and Interviewing Officers. Selection centre allocation and interview instructions will be communicated to shortlisted candidates through the registered email address, SMS and official recruitment system. The TES-57 final merit list is prepared on the basis of SSB marks. Higher academic qualifications, previous performance and NCC background do not provide additional merit-list weightage. Final joining depends on medical fitness, the candidate's merit position, fulfillment of eligibility conditions and available vacancies.

content_sections.heading: Indian Army TES 57 Training Period 2027
content_sections.text: Selected candidates will undergo four years of integrated military and engineering training. The programme consists of three years at a Cadets Training Wing and one year at the Indian Military Academy, Dehradun. Candidates who successfully complete the four-year training programme will be awarded an Engineering degree. Candidates recommended by the SSB must submit preferences for all three Cadets Training Wings. Final allocation is decided by the Indian Army.

faq.question: When does Indian Army TES 57 registration start?
faq.answer: The online registration window opens on 14 October 2026 at 12:00 noon.

faq.question: What is the educational qualification for Indian Army TES 57?
faq.answer: Candidates must have passed Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, secured at least 60% aggregate marks in PCM and appeared in JEE Main 2026.

faq.question: Is JEE Main compulsory for Indian Army TES 57 Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Yes. Appearance in JEE Main 2026 is mandatory. The Army uses the JEE Main 2026 Common Rank List for shortlisting.

faq.question: Can candidates with 60% PCM marks apply for TES 57?
faq.answer: Yes. Candidates with at least 60% aggregate marks in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics in Class 12 can apply if they satisfy the JEE Main, age and other eligibility conditions.

faq.question: What is the age limit for Indian Army TES 57?
faq.answer: Candidates must be between 16 years 6 months and 19 years 6 months as on 1 July 2027. The eligible date-of-birth range is 1 January 2008 to 1 January 2011, both dates inclusive.

faq.question: Can female candidates apply for Indian Army TES 57?
faq.answer: No. The TES-57 notification invites applications from unmarried male candidates.

faq.question: What is the selection process for Indian Army TES 57?
faq.answer: Selection includes shortlisting based on JEE Main 2026 CRL, a five-day SSB interview, medical examination and final merit list. Joining is subject to eligibility and available vacancies.

faq.question: Is there a separate written examination for Indian Army TES 57?
faq.answer: The notification does not prescribe a separate recruitment written examination. Shortlisting is based on JEE Main 2026 CRL, followed by SSB and medical assessment.

content_sections.text: Only Indian Nationals are eligible to apply. The essential qualification for the Data Entry Operator post has three parts: Minimum 12th passed from a recognized board/institution. Well conversant with computer packages namely Windows, i.e. Word, Excel course of DOEACC or equivalent from any Govt. / Recognized private institute, with good working knowledge of Computer and internet/E-mail. Typing speed of more than 35 words per minute (English) on computer. Preference: Preference may be given to candidates with higher qualifications, superior academic credentials, additional relevant experience or any other desirable criteria, as determined by the Client/Principal Employer. Preference may also be given to local candidates and/or candidates with relevant experience in the same or similar department, subject to the requirements of the Client/Principal Employer. Not eligible: Candidates previously engaged by BECIL and/or the Client are not eligible if their services were terminated, discontinued or not renewed on account of disciplinary action, misconduct, unsatisfactory performance or violation of contractual terms.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for BECIL Data Entry Operator
content_sections.text: The application must be submitted online through the BECIL application portal, along with all requisite documents as specified against the eligibility criteria of the post. The notice gives these steps: Visit https://becilregistration.in to complete the online registration process. Fill in the personal details under new registration and register. Proceed to the other details and payment to complete the application submission process. Pay the application processing fee for your category, as shown in the table below. Save the application receipt after the online payment is successful. The fee once paid is non-refundable and non-transferable under any circumstances. A candidate applying for more than one post must submit a separate application and pay the fee separately for each post. BECIL does not demand or accept any payment at any stage of the recruitment process other than the prescribed Application Processing Fee, wherever applicable.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: BECIL first scrutinises the applications, then forwards a shortlist to the Client/Principal Employer, who decides the further selection process. Scrutiny and shortlisting: Applications are scrutinised and shortlisted on the eligibility criteria prescribed for the post. BECIL reserves the right to adopt suitable shortlisting criteria, including but not limited to higher qualifications, greater relevant experience or any other criteria deemed appropriate. No automatic call: Possessing the prescribed qualifications, experience and other requirements does not entitle a candidate to be called for any stage of selection. Further selection: The further process includes interview, assessment, skill test or any other evaluation method as may be decided by the Client. Intimation: Shortlisted candidates are told the date, time and venue/mode of the interview, assessment or skill test (if any) through registered email and/or telephone. Result: Candidates selected by the Client/Principal Employer are informed of their selection and subsequent formalities through email and/or telephone. BECIL is not obliged to publish interim results, stage-wise shortlists or marks. Only the final result, listing the selected candidates, is published on the official website of BECIL. Decisions of the Client/Principal Employer and BECIL on eligibility, shortlisting, selection and engagement are final and binding, and no correspondence on them is entertained.

content_sections.text: Applications submitted after this date and time will not be considered and will be summarily rejected. No request to extend the last date will be entertained.

Under SCL Technical Assistant Recruitment 2026 , 30 vacancies are available across 11 technical disciplines. Candidates must possess the prescribed First Class Diploma, B.Sc. or other accepted qualification with two years of relevant post-qualification experience . The SCL Technician 'B' Recruitment 2026 includes 41 vacancies for ITI-qualified candidates in various technical trades. content_sections.heading: SCL Recruitment 2026 Eligibility and Qualification
content_sections.text: The educational qualification and experience requirements for SCL Recruitment 2026 depend on the selected post. Candidates should verify the specific eligibility conditions before applying. Important: The administrative officer posts require relevant supervisory experience. For Technical Assistant and Technician 'B', the prescribed experience must be obtained after completing the qualifying education. Candidates should read the post-specific conditions in the detailed notification. For most Technical Assistant disciplines, candidates must possess a First Class three-year full-time Diploma in the respective engineering field with two years of post-qualification experience. For Electronics, SCL also accepts a First Class B.Sc. in Electronics. For Computer Science, the notification provides an alternative through First Class BCA / Computer Science qualifications. For Physics and Chemistry, candidates need the prescribed First Class B.Sc. qualification in the relevant subject. Technician 'B' applicants must have passed Matriculation / SSLC and completed the prescribed two-year ITI course from an NCVT-recognized institution in the respective trade, or hold an accepted National Apprenticeship Certificate / National Trade Certificate. Two years of relevant post-qualification experience is also required. Candidates applying for Junior Personal Assistant must have passed Class 12 from a recognized board. The stenography requirement includes 10 minutes of dictation at 80 words per minute and transcription on a computer within 50 minutes for English or 65 minutes for Hindi.
